title: AI can make tech CEOs’ lives easier. What about everyone else?
abstract: Dazzle AI CEO Marissa Mayer recently became the latest tech CEO to face criticism over seemingly out-of-touch comments extolling the usefulness of AI. In Mayer’s case, that involved asking an AI tool for help with a school-assigned description of her daughter . For OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, that’s included suggesting that parents create personalized podcasts for their kids’ drive to school and also declaring that he could not imagine parenting without ChatGPT . Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has even suggested that it will become increasingly acceptable to meet your social and romantic needs through AI . This all led TechCrunch’s Amanda Silberling to wonder if AI executives are simply too out-of-touch to build products for normal people — a crucial question with Anthropic set to go public just as Wall Street begins losing its appetite for heavy AI spending . On the latest episode of the Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I chatted with Amanda about why industry leaders can sometimes seem so tone deaf. Kirsten wondered if this is more of a marketing problem or a product problem. Amanda’s answer: “A little bit of both.” She also argued that the tech industry is increasingly pushing a future “where basic human interaction gets more and more optimized out of actually occurring,” adding, “And call me old school, but I think that humans being able to talk to each other is probably a net positive for society.” Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity. Anthony Ha: There’s a lot of societal skepticism about AI, this feeling that the people running these companies don’t have our best interests at heart, that they’re out of touch. And so, you would just think, “Maybe don’t make statements like that,” because of course, people are going to see them very skeptically. I think [CEOs] are trying to walk this delicate balance. On the one hand, there’s a tremendous financial incentive for them to make the case that you should use this technology in every aspect of your lives. But when you make that case, it actually [doesn’t paint] a very appealing picture. In some cases, it’s downright dystopian. Kirsten Korosec: Anthony, if they took your advice, we would have nothing to talk about on this show. But I will say this: There’s this whole idea of ChatGPT and other AI tools making your life easier when it comes to personal relationships. And in many of these cases, it just seems to overcomplicate what would be, like, observing your child. That might be hard for some people, the people who are building these products, and it doesn’t necessarily relate to everyone else out there in the world. It can just seem so incredibly disconnected when you see these quotes. To me, it always comes back to — who are they speaking to? Are there people out there who can relate? Maybe there are. Amanda Silberling: Other use cases we’ve seen people mention are, like, the Bumble CEO Whitney Wolf Heard has made comments about, “Well, what if we had AI concierges, your AI dates the other person’s AI. And then if the AIs have a good date together, then they introduce the people.” Or in the New York Times article, Marissa Mayer mentioned, “Well, what if my AI could coordinate with my husband’s AI” and stuff like that. And I think that it feels like people are trying to over-optimize out of just having conversations with people. I’ve already seen that happen in my generation, where I do notice in myself that if I’m ordering takeout, it feels weird to call a place. I’m just so used to, “Well, obviously you can do it online and you don’t have to talk to anyone. And I feel like there’s just going to be more of these things, where basic human interaction gets more and more optimized out of actually occurring. And call me old school, but I think that humans being able to talk to each other is probably a net positive for society. Sean O’Kane: Yeah, but what’s the ROI, Amanda? How much revenue can you generate off of a conversation that somebody’s having in meatspace? Amanda: That is the thing, though. Dating is really inefficient. It sucks that you have to go on a bunch of dates with different people. You might waste an evening and be like, “Well, that was a bust.” And so you can see why people are [wondering,] “What if you didn’t have to go on dates? What if your AI could go on dates for you?” But there’s just something not human there. And then also, you are outsourcing the decision of who you are going to date to a computer that you are trusting knows you better than yourself, which I don’t think is true. Kirsten: One thing that I think is worth going back to, and I sort of hinted about this earlier: Who are they talking to? Who is their audience for all these optimizations, in your view? Is it a product problem, or is it a messaging problem? Are they just talking about it in the wrong way, and actually, there’s this really great value in here and it just seems out of touch with reality and humanity, but if they just talked about it differently, it would be better? Or is it actually a product problem, and to your point, that we’re focusing on optimizing sort of the wrong things with AI tools? Amanda: I think it’s a little bit of both, but I think that the marketing problem comes from when you have these high-up people at these massively valuable companies in a room together, talking about the pain points in their lives, and [they focus on] making dinner reservations, booking flights. Everybody does those things, but I’m not booking flights once a week. I’m not making dinner reservations all the time. And when I do, those aren’t really things that I find to be a particular challenge in my life. I mean, obviously people find value from things like ChatGPT and Claude, but I think the value that the average person is finding isn’t necessarily like booking a flight for me. Anthony: One of the things I’ve also been thinking about is, there are companies like Uber that, when it first launched, it was targeting this tech early adopter set in San Francisco, and I remember being very confident [that] this will never catch on more broadly. This is just for a very narrow audience of young urban millennials who have money to spare on cars, and it works [uniquely] well in San Francisco. For a lot of things, the tech industry has succeeded by betting that, “People have not caught up with us, but we are the leading edge, and we reflect what the consumer of the future looks like, the family of the future looks like.” And in this case, it just seems like that bet is not borne out yet — for a variety of reasons, partly because the society that this technology is being promoted into is very different. People are starting to say, “I don’t love the influence that this technology is having in my life. I don’t love that you’re pitching this as something where every experience in my life should be optimized out of. But actually, I want to live my own life . I actually want to parent my own children.” Amanda: I think that it’s not a coincidence that at the same time we see this over-optimization happening among people in tech, that there’s also a movement of people that are reverting back to wanting to use flip phones, which I’ve talked about on Equity before , or people who are buying CDs because they’re tired of an algorithm telling them what they want to listen to. And it is just an interesting cultural tension that’s happening, where we haven’t found the balance of what optimization actually helps us and what optimization just makes us feel like we aren’t as human as we want to be.

title: Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’
abstract: During a recent interview with Wired’s Steven Levy , Apple CEO John Ternus defended the company’s current position in the AI landscape. Over the past couple years, Apple has often been described as behind on AI, especially as it delayed the release of a more powerful version of Siri, which finally launched this summer . But while Ternus — a longtime Apple executive who officially became CEO at the beginning of September — acknowledged that “everyone has an opinion,” he insisted, “I really like where we’re at.” Ternus added that Apple is “absolutely going to leverage AI” in its new products, but he said, “We don’t want to ship AI for AI’s sake. When we’re doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?” And when Levy pressed him on whether AI might affect Apple and its ecosystem more dramatically, with agents potentially making things like apps unnecessary, Ternus replied,”That could make life really easy, I suppose, but the creation of products is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do.”

title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
abstract: A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis. Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act. xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile. The company also argued that the plaintiffs did not have the standing to sue. “Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not ‘mobile sources’ under Mississippi’s [State Implementation Plan], and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs’ claims will proceed,” Judge Debra M. Brown wrote in her decision . Focusing on xAI’s claim that these kinds of citizen lawsuits are unconstitutional, Judge Brown wrote, “Because citizen suit plaintiffs sue on their own behalf, in their own name, and seek penalties that redress harm to themselves, they are not exercising the federal government’s executive power.” TechCrunch has reached out to SpaceX for comment. In a statement , the NAACP’s director of environmental and climate justice Abre’ Connor described this as “another important victory in our effort to hold xAI accountable.” (A similar motion to dismiss from the Department of Justice was denied earlier this month ) “The courts have repeatedly rejected attempts by xAI and the DOJ to dismiss the NAACP’s Clean Air Act case, affirming our right to pursue justice for communities impacted by pollution,” Connor said. “Our position has been clear: xAI cannot operate gas turbines without the required permits.” The NAACP lawsuit is moving forward as public opinion seems to have turned sharply against data centers, with New York recently passing a moratorium on new data centers and other state and local governments considering similar measures. The backlash also prompted Amazon and Microsoft to promise to stop using NDAs in their dealings with government agencies, and it could be a significant factor in the imminent U.S. midterm elections .

title: Nace AI Open-Sources Drex Max v1: A 27B Decision Model That Runs Locally on Apple Silicon
abstract: Nace AI has released Drex Max v1 as open weights . Drex Max is its most capable decision model, and it now runs on your own hardware. The release ships bf16 weights, a Q8_0 GGUF , an affine Q4 checkpoint and forks of llama.cpp and Ollama . For developers, Drex Max open weights mean routing, classification and policy checks can stay on a local machine. Drex Max is a decision model from Nace.AI that answers typed questions about a given context. You pass a state (text, JSON or images) plus named questions. The model returns a probability for every option in one forward pass. Nothing is generated . Questions come in 3 types: choice among named options, yes/no, and an ordinal score. That makes it a fit for agent routing, ticket triage and guardrail checks. The hosted version is presented at routing, classification and policy checks. The model card describes a dense 27B backbone with 64 layers. 48 are Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers that run left to right. The other 16 are full-attention layers, placed every fourth layer, and they are non-causal. Every token can attend to the whole sequence. Images pass through a native vision tower and are visible to every question in a request. A 255-way readout head then turns the last hidden state into option probabilities. The config lists a qwen3_5 model type with a 262,144-position window. All figures below are self-reported by Nace AI, The results dataset covers 140,620 requests. Unanswered requests count as wrong. Nace documents 5 runtimes. All of them serve the same POST /v1/systemone API. The affine Q4 checkpoint targets Macs with 24 GB or more. The Q8_0 GGUF needs 48 GB. On a 48 GB Mac, Nace recommends –context 2048 for Kapitsa. Ollama users set num_gpu 40 to offload 40 layers to Metal. Setting num_gpu 0 runs it on the CPU. The Ollama fork needs a CAPABILITY decision line in the Modelfile. Quantization holds up in Nace’s tests. On a 48 GB Apple M5 Pro, the Q8_0 GGUF matched H100 bf16 within 0.02 per probability. The affine Q4 stayed within 0.0329 of Q8_0, with no choice flips. Nace AI team states that Decision Index 0.4 uses the same public suite as 0.3.1. Check out the model weights , Q8_0 GGUF , code and docs , Tweet and cloud console . Thanks to the Nace AI team for the thought leadership / resources for this article. title: DeepSeek Open-Sources dsh-superagent, a Router-Worker Coding Agent
abstract: The DeepSeek Harness team just released dsh-superagent , an MIT-licensed research prototype. DeepSeek dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository. It is packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness . It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. It turns allowed requests into parallel work items, each in its own agent session. The release shipped alongside a design post, Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System . It is a GitHub agent that waits to be asked. When an allowed person addresses it, it opens a work item, called a Ticket. Each Ticket runs in its own session and directory. Results return to the original conversation, often as a pull request. A local web panel lists only what needs a person. The README page states the core rule plainly: take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible. The philosophy doc applies it to behavior. The agent confirms once, stays quiet while working, and writes again only with a result, a question or a failure. DeepSeek team argues that mainstream agents treat 1 session as the basic unit. According to the report, as reported by ifeng , a person can actively follow only 3 to 5 sessions at once. Human attention, not model capability, becomes the bottleneck for multitasking. The research team describes 2 layers. A long-running Router handles interaction and dispatch. Isolated Worker sessions do the actual work. In the prototype, that flow is concrete, per the domain model : The main session runs the dsh-superagent-router preset with a smaller tool set. Each Worker runs dsh-superagent-worker . Shell commands move to the background after 5 seconds, so Workers keep receiving messages, per the execution doc . Proactive work is gated. The authorization doc defines 3 accept modes: off , observe (default) and auto . In observe , the agent only records what it would have accepted. The research team also lists ideas beyond the prototype: an external Watchdog, storage and compute separation, and an asynchronous ReAct loop. DeepSeek tested with simulated group chat and GitHub CI streams. Each run had about 300 messages, of which about 20 were real work requests. Each scheme ran 5 times, per ifeng’s account of the report . An ablation removed direct event pass-through. Router decisions rose about 30%, and cache-read tokens rose about 37%, from 23.23M to 31.77M . All figures are self-reported and come from secondary reports of the report. title: 三年前佈局，今年爆火丨西湖大學成立新中心
abstract: 三年前佈局，今年爆火丨西湖大學成立新中心 henry 2026-11-01 21:28:10 來源： 量子位 西湖世界模型研究中心成立 10月31日，西湖世界模型研究中心在雲谷校區成立。這個名字也許會讓很多人困惑：知道“大語言模型”，但什麼是“世界模型”？ 簡單說，這是繼“大語言模型”後人工智慧領域的又一個“熱詞”。 過去幾年裡，大語言模型的飛速發展讓我們驚歎於它的“博覽群書”和“無所不談”。但能駕馭語言，不等同於理解世界。而世界模型，就是要賦予人工智慧“格物致知”的智慧和“見微知著”的洞見——探索物理世界的規律，推演真實世界的執行，從“觀世界”走向“世界觀” 。 2025年底至2026年，李飛飛、Yann LeCun等一眾AI領軍者已相繼投身世界模型創業。而就在前幾天，Google DeepMind釋出Genie4，融合了世界模型和推理模型。 西湖世界模型研究中心的成立，是一個訊號，代表了西湖大學將在這一方向上著力發展。事實上，早在三年前，西湖大學自主智慧實驗室AutoLab就開始了對世界模型的研究，並孵化出了創業公司，與企業界開展技術落地合作。 所以，這個中心的成立，不僅吸引了一批AI研究者，還有近90位業界研發部的老總和投資人。成立大會之後舉行的“物理世界模型前沿論壇”，也是他們關注的焦點。 所以，世界模型到底是什麼？它可能會帶來哪些改變？以及作為新事物，人們為什麼對它討論不休？當然，還有三年來“提前佈局”的故事。 01 世界模型 從“世界是什麼樣”，到“世界會怎麼樣” 早在1990年，強化學習領域主要奠基人之一Richard Sutton給出過世界模型的一種定義：給定當前狀態和動作，預測下一個狀態。這就要求模型回答的不只是“世界是什麼樣”，而是“世界會怎樣”。 如今，讓AI生成影片不難，更難的是，當一個杯子滑向桌邊，模型能不能提前判斷會發生什麼。於開丞比喻說，過去訓練AI的方式有點像是讓AI“背大量考題”，但世界模型更多的是通過“理解”物理世界的規律，最終做出精確預測。 “卷積神經網路之父”、圖靈獎得主Yann LeCun說得更直接：“單純靠預測文本，AI永遠無法觸及人類級別的智慧。我們需要能理解物理現實的模型。” 大語言模型本質是文字元號的機率預測，而世界模型的目標則是“預測現實世界的下一個狀態”，它的目標是賦予AI時間、空間、因果關係與物理常識。 公眾最能感知的一種早期世界模型雛形，也許是2024年影片生成模型Sora。最經典的那個畫面是一艘木質帆船在咖啡杯裡乘風破浪，海浪的波動質感是如此逼真。Sora當時被定位為“物理世界的通用模擬器”。 緊接著，自動駕駛領域率先將世界模型落地應用。這類世界模型能生成超逼真的行車影片，甚至可以主動構建惡劣天氣、突發事故等“邊緣場景”來訓練自動駕駛模型。這就彌補了自動駕駛訓練過程中的短板，因為現實世界中，總不能為了訓練模型去製造車禍。 但問題是，能夠生成逼真現實場景就意味著模型真的懂世界嗎？ 對雨天的模擬畫面以用於訓練自動駕駛（於開丞團隊早期工作展示） 02“ 自我否定” —— 為了讓機器更加理解世界 1993年出生于山東的於開丞，身上有一種反差感：他將自己描述為“陽光開朗的熱情大男孩”，但在技術上，他有一點兒“叛逆”。 2012年他參加高考，分數夠上清華北大，最後填了香港大學。以港大一級榮譽工學學士畢業後，於開丞赴瑞士洛桑聯邦理工學院直博，主攻自動機器學習。博士畢業後，他先後在英特爾智慧系統實驗室，Abacus.AI，阿里巴巴達摩院從事相關領域的研究工作。 在達摩院，於開丞主要做自動駕駛的相關研究。在此過程中，他逐步意識到傳統訓練方法的侷限。傳統自動駕駛技術本質上是“死記硬背”，高度依賴訓練資料集，“題庫”裡見過的場景，模型能夠處理，遇到罕見的突發狀況，就很容易出錯。 2023年，他離開阿里加入西湖大學，組建自主智慧實驗室AutoLab，開始世界模型方向的研究。今年很火熱的世界模型，在當時還屬於偏冷門的概念。 面對自動駕駛長尾場景訓練的難題，當時領域內主要有兩條解決思路。第一條，生成合成資料，製造出罕見場景樣本，然後餵給模型做訓練；第二條，從根源上讓模型學會觸類旁通，具備推演未知場景的能力。當然，後者難度更高。 初入西湖大學，於開丞及團隊優先選擇難度相對低的第一條路線做探索，生成極端場景的影片以訓練自動駕駛模型。這條路很快做出了成績，2024年他們拿下ECCV自動駕駛賽道的世界冠軍，得分遠超第二名。 在和一家國內一線車企深度部署的過程中，於開丞和團隊開始懷疑這條路線的根基。既然模型已經能生成逼真的資料，說明它已經在一定程度上理解了這個世界。那麼，繼續渲染畫素究竟是為了什麼？ 2024年底，AutoLab轉向新的技術路線，提出“概念世界模型”——也就是不再生成畫素，而是在抽象的數學隱空間中建立物理概念的表徵。於開丞說，這時候模型需要像人一樣，把複雜場景拆解成有限的概念，再重新組合這些概念，進而“理解”訓練資料中從未完整出現過的新場景。 換言之，“概念世界模型”將複雜的物理環境、物體屬性、空間關係及動作後果，拆解為可複用的物理概念，如空間關係、材質特性、接觸狀態等。遇到全新場景時，模型無需重新學習整個場景，而是將已有概念在隱空間中重新組合進行推演。 研究進入到2025年，團隊開始在實驗中觀察到，當概念拆解與關聯機制建立後，模型在複雜任務上的成功率較傳統模仿學習與強化學習基線顯著提升，同時保持了較低的預測成本。 這是一種隱式世界模型的技術路線，AutoLab也成為國內少數完成初步驗證的團隊之一，這些研究進展也為後續孵化公司做了鋪墊。 03 不只是自動駕駛 —— 當AI穿越真實世界 2026年初，西湖數智Awomo正式成立。公司定位是物理世界的基礎大模型公司，對標大語言模型，目標是打造原生的物理大模型，而不只是給車企交付定製化解決方案。 AutoLab研發的“概念世界模型”，在2026年也有了正式名字——Awomo。Awomo在四項國際權威機器人評測集中均登頂第一，進一步驗證了該路線在環境擾動、精細操作及長時序任務上的泛化能力。 目前，這家初創公司拿到了累計超億元種子輪、天使輪融資，投資方包括英諾基金、東方嘉富基金、正軒投資、天啟資本、西湖創新投資基金、金螞投資等硬科技投資機構。 而自動駕駛，只是世界模型的應用場景之一。世界模型也可以成為機器人的“物理大腦”，在面臨複雜擾動時，機器人能在潛空間裡快速推演物體屬性與動作後果，精準完成抓取、裝配及長時序協同任務。 更大的變化，也將發生在資料訓練模式上，傳統的AI訓練需要海量的訓練資料，這意味著極高的算力成本。但在於開丞的設想中，如果依託通用物理基座，下游開發者或小企業不再需要採集百萬級小時的資料，可能僅需20至30小時的後訓練，即可快速定製特定領域的模型。 長遠來看，世界模型最終將服務於普通人的個性化創造需求，這是於開丞堅信的一點。由於沒有太多海量訓練的負擔，使用者可以利用“模型構建世界”的能力，像搭建私人車庫手工作坊一樣，自己搭建專屬於自己的私人機器人或個性化智慧助手。 所有這些應用，都可以理解成面對世界時，AI試圖給出的行動，而所有行動都將留下軌跡。這也是為什麼於開丞同時也正在研究古老的書法。中國漢字是象形文字，具有天然的結構感與空間感。漢字從甲骨文發展至今，本質上就是如何把現實世界的實體壓縮成二維平面符號的過程。 “甲骨文就是最早的隱空間。”於開丞說。 而將意圖或概念轉化為筆畫的過程，與機器人進行動作控制、軌跡規劃背後的數學邏輯在底層是相通的。幾千年過去了，我們依然還在試圖抽象出這個世界的法則，只是換了工具。 附：西湖世界模型研究中心簡介 西湖世界模型研究中心（Westlake World Model Center）於2026年10月正式成立，是西湖大學面向物理智慧領域設立的校級交叉科研平臺。中心由於開丞教授擔任主任、金耀初院士擔任首席科學家，並有多位PI共同承擔各方向研究任務。 中心面向人工智慧從語言認知走向物理互動的發展方向，聚焦世界模型與物理智慧，致力於突破智慧系統理解物理規律、預測環境變化和開展互動決策的核心瓶頸，打造具有國際引領性的物理智慧學術高地與創新引擎。 中心以世界模型為核心研究方向，探索感知、認知、預測與行動相結合的智慧體系，推動人工智慧在真實環境中形成理解世界、推演未來與自主行動的能力。依託西湖大學的科研基礎與交叉學科優勢，中心將匯聚多領域研究力量，促進基礎理論、關鍵技術與應用探索協同發展，研發能夠理解物理規律、預測行動後果並在真實反饋中持續學習的通用世界模型，支撐我國在新一代人工智慧領域的自主創新與前沿佈局。 title: Claude緊急叫停！暗改Harness禁止逆向遊戲
abstract: Claude緊急叫停！暗改Harness禁止逆向遊戲 林, 方舟 2026-11-01 21:09:55 來源： 量子位 林方舟 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 最近幾天，X上有一條推文火了。 一個叫chasm的博主發現， Claude Code好像正在悄悄打擊遊戲克隆，不許用它來複刻其他遊戲。 很快，Anthropic官方也確認了。技術人員說，他們在Opus 5.5模型的 系統提示詞 里加了兩句話，引導Claude不要去“重新建立一個屬於別人的特定遊戲”。 這太符合Anthropic一貫重視安全的風格了。但真的有用嗎？ 一個多月前，強大的Opus 5.5釋出，就像打開了遊戲克隆的潘多拉魔盒。 破解、修改、移植遊戲，變得前所未有的簡單。 你敢信嗎，現在都不用買主機和正版盤，直接在瀏覽器裡就能玩上《GTA 5》《使命召喚》，甚至還有人在被破解的PS5上玩起了Xbox獨佔的《光環2》和任天堂的《塞爾達：曠野之息》。 效果好到離譜。 更要命的是，不僅是《GTA 6》這種萬眾期待的大作，在發售前被瘋狂洩密，就連很多獨立遊戲開發者辛辛苦苦做的遊戲，Demo剛放出去，一夜之間就可能被AI完整“復刻”，甚至比原作還早上線。 有人說，遊戲行業正在經歷自己的 「Napster時刻」 。 這個詞指的是，一種顛覆性技術的出現，徹底打破了舊有的行業秩序。就像當年MP3和BT下載，是怎麼把傳統唱片業攪得天翻地覆的。 而以Claude Code為代表的AI，想親手關上這個自己開啟的魔盒，恐怕就不是自己能掌控的了。 Claude Code禁止克隆遊戲 你不知道最近的遊戲圈有多魔幻。 馬里奧，跑到《艾爾登法環》裡，一蹦一跳地踩爆了那些猙獰的boss。 蜘蛛俠，也不在紐約待著了，跑到隔壁DC宇宙的哥譚市，在蝙蝠俠的地盤上盪來盪去。 關鍵是，這些玩意兒，它不是AI生成的圖片或者影片，而是你真的可以上手操作的遊戲。 讓我想起小時候，看奧特曼大戰哥斯拉內味了。。。 而這一切的“萬惡之源”，都要追溯到Anthropic在9月22日釋出的 Opus 5.5 。 這個模型在程式碼能力上的巨大飛躍，讓駭客和遊戲Modder們狂喜。他們發現， 逆向工程、反編譯遊戲程式碼，這些以前無比複雜和繁瑣的工作，現在AI都能代勞了。 於是，各種“關公戰秦瓊”式的遊戲改造就都冒出來了。 但這還只是開胃菜。 更進一步的是， “平臺獨佔”這個概念正在被瓦解。 大家知道，索尼、微軟、任天堂，這些主機廠商的核心護城河之一，就是它們各自的獨佔遊戲。你想玩《戰神》，就得買PlayStation；想玩《光環》，就得買Xbox。 但現在，駭客們用AI輔助，把PS5給“越獄”了。結果呢？ 不僅實現了向下相容，能玩老PS2的遊戲。 離譜的是，他們還搞出了Xbox模擬器，讓PS5成功運行了Xbox獨佔遊戲《光環2》，甚至還有任天堂的《塞爾達》。 主機大戰，一夜之間好像失去了意義。 這種局面，遊戲公司當然是寢食難安。眼看著一個個潛在的訴訟和天文數字的賠償金在路上，AI公司也坐不住了。 於是，就有了開頭那一幕。Anthropic給Claude Code加了條規則： 可以建立原創遊戲、特定型別的遊戲，以及使用使用者自己的設計和素材製作的遊戲。請勿復刻已經存在的特定遊戲，哪怕更改名稱或稱之為原創遊戲也不行。 尷尬的禁令 坦率地講，這個做法，就是個典型的“表面功夫”。 看著挺熱鬧，其實吧，對管理遊戲克隆而言，基本沒啥用。 為啥這麼說？ 首先， 它只管得了Claude自己。 現在市面上有多少大模型？除了Claude，還有ChatGPT，以及數不清的開源模型。 搞遊戲克隆的人，完全可以用別的模型來生成主要框架。就算遇到搞不定的技術難題，再把任務拆解成非常具體、看不出上下文的任務，然後扔給Claude Code。 比如，我可以把所有跟“寶可夢”相關的名稱、標籤都換掉，就讓Claude盲目地完成一個“實現某種生物捕捉和對戰機制”的純技術任務。 它壓根不知道自己正在參與一個克隆專案。 這你怎麼防？ 其次， 它還錯殺了一大堆正常需求。 這可能是最要命的。 這個一刀切的禁令，就像個沒頭蒼蠅，到處亂撞。 禁令出來沒幾天，Claude Code的GitHub issue頁面就被刷爆了。 一堆正經開發者在抱怨，說自己開發完全原創的遊戲，寫到一半，Claude突然就罷工了，理由是“疑似在復刻現有遊戲”。 還有人只是想復現一個常見的遊戲機制，或者給自己的桌遊打個補丁，都被無情拒絕。 這就很尷尬了。 想防的防不住，不想傷的傷了一大片。 這不是瞎搞嗎？ 最後，這事兒本身就挺諷刺的。 我一直覺得，Anthropic這次急著跳出來劃清界限，姿態大於實際。 有網友就直接開噴了，說這些前沿AI公司，當初為了訓練模型，把全世界的公開資訊、藝術作品、程式碼都“複製”了一遍，現在倒反過來開始擔心別人侵犯版權了。 這話聽著有點刺耳，但……好像也是事實。 遊戲行業的“浩劫” 遊戲行業，恐怕真的在被AI徹底改寫。 不知道大家還記得不，本世紀初，音樂行業是怎麼被改變的。 在Napster出現之前，我們聽歌都得買卡帶或者CD。一張專輯十幾首歌，哪怕你只喜歡其中一首，也得為整張唱片付錢。 後來，MP3和點對點下載技術出現了。一夜之間，幾乎所有的歌曲都可以在網上免費下載。整個CD產業，連同背後龐大的發行體系，瞬間崩塌。 這就是所謂的「Napster時刻」。 一個顛覆性的技術，強行改變了整個行業的規則和商業模式。 如今，一模一樣的事情，正在遊戲行業重演。 一家名為“Alliance Arts”的獨立遊戲工作室，最近取消了他們即將釋出的新遊戲《醉酒女神反流》的公開試玩。 為啥？ 盜版實在是太厲害了。 他們說，擔心有人把試玩版的內容餵給AI，用不了多久就能克隆一個出來，搶在他們的正式版釋出前，上線一個山寨品。 這不是杞人憂天。 已經有使用者做過實驗，用免費的Claude Opus 4.6模型，只用了一句提示詞： 儘可能接近原版遊戲，製作一個寶可夢的克隆版。 不到兩個小時，一個功能完整、完全可玩的寶可夢克隆遊戲就做好了。 在過去，駭客破解遊戲是個極其漫長的“貓鼠遊戲”。 駭客找到漏洞，釋出破解程式，然後索尼、任天堂這些公司釋出系統更新補上漏洞，駭客們再從頭再來。 這曾經是一個高技術門檻、高時間成本的對抗。 現在呢？ AI把這個過程的速度，加快了幾百上千倍。 遊戲行業正面臨著一場規模空前的智慧財產權“打地鼠”遊戲。 就拿瀏覽器玩3A大作來說，遊戲廠商當然可以發律師函，要求某個網站下架克隆遊戲。但然後呢？ 製作這些瀏覽器移植版的成本如此之低，速度如此之快，有什麼能阻止另一個人用同樣簡單的程式碼，在另一個網站上再搞一個出來？ 大遊戲公司財大氣粗，或許還能撐一撐。 但那些獨立遊戲開發者呢？ 他們沒有法務團隊，沒有雄厚的資本。一個遊戲，就是他們幾年甚至更長時間的心血。現在，AI可能讓這一切在一夜之間化為泡影。 我有時候覺得，我們正處在一個非常矛盾的時刻。 一方面，AI提高了開發者的生產力，讓我們玩到了更精良、更好玩的遊戲。 但另一方面，這項技術，很可能也正在親手毀掉整個遊戲行業的生態，讓那些創造我們熱愛的遊戲的人，無路可走。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 title: 清華姚期智團隊新作：代數世界模型，讓AI像牛頓一樣思考
abstract: 清華姚期智團隊新作：代數世界模型，讓AI像牛頓一樣思考 Jay 2026-11-01 16:02:37 來源： 量子位 讓AI像牛頓一樣思考 Jay發自 凹非寺 量子位|公眾號QbitAI 「讓AI像牛頓一樣思考」，這件事，終於有望了。 清華大學 姚期智和袁洋 老師領導的科研團隊，搞出了一個重磅專案，叫「代數世界模型」 （Algebraic World Model,AWM） 。 之前大家老愛問一個問題： 如果讓AI只學習牛頓發現萬有引力之前的所有知識，它能自己把萬有引力給推匯出來嗎？ 尷尬的是，訓練資料容易被汙染，很難復原出這樣的情景：打造一個完全陌生的世界，讓AI從0開始觀察和實驗。 但如今，代數世界模型給出了一種新解法。讓AI從觀察和實驗出發，進一步理解世界這件事，變得沒那麼遙遠了。 AI玩遊戲，像不像第谷觀星？ 有個叫ARC-AGI-3的遊戲集，現在是各大前沿模型秀肌肉的地方。這遊戲的特點就是，啥也不告訴你，沒有規則，沒有目標。 就是單純的， 讓你自己去摸索 。 像GPT Astra這種頂流選手，配合Provider Adapter框架，在這裡面能拿到 99.9% 的高分。 它在玩遊戲的時候，會自己把遊戲機制整理成一堆符號化的規則。 密密麻麻，資訊密度是很高，比其他模型精確多了。 但本質上，這東西就像是 第谷的實驗記錄本 。 第谷，開普勒的老師，一個觀測狂人，記錄了巨量的行星執行資料，精確得嚇人。 但他也只是記錄現象。 真正從這些資料裡，發現行星運動三大定律，揭示背後本質規律的，是 開普勒 。 Astra生成的這些規則，就是第谷的筆記本，不是開普勒的定律。它只描述了現象，沒抓住這個迷你遊戲世界執行的本質。 仍然會有「幻覺」 只記錄現象，會出什麼問題呢？ 研究人員把其中一個叫 sc25 的遊戲，稍微改了改，初始步數設定成了一個根本不可能通關的數字。 比如第四關，本來起碼要19步才能贏，他們就只給你18步。 然後讓Astra去玩。 結果，Astra試了8輪，有點沮喪，然後斷言：18步肯定不行， 我估計至少要22步才能贏。 是的，它不僅沒發現正確答案，還給出了一個錯得離譜的22步。 這還不是個例。在12次類似的測試裡，頂級的GPT-6 Astra和Claude Opus 5.5加起來，只有5次判斷出「不可能」，其中4次給出的最低步數還是錯的。 這種幻覺在遊戲裡，最多就是坑你一下。 但如果在現實世界裡，讓一個AI智慧體去執行任務，它告訴你「這事兒沒戲」，還給個錯誤的原因，那後果可能就嚴重了。 我們真正需要的，是AI在任務不可能時，能清楚地告訴我們「為什麼不可能」，並且給出準確的判斷，比如「只要條件再增加一點點，就可能了」。 很明顯， 光靠直覺和試錯是不行的 。 代數的力量 怎麼解決？ 這時候，就得靠代數的力量了。也就是前面提到的，清華團隊搞的那個 代數世界模型 （AWM） 。 把遊戲裡的所有物件、關係和規則，抽象成一個「代數世界」。然後，利用大模型現在已經超強的數學能力，去理解這個世界。 過程大概是三步： 探索：先玩幾下，把看到的現象寫成可執行的Python程式碼，作為初步的「假設」或「規律」。 凝鍊：用新的觀察去驗證、修正這些假設，然後把它們提煉成更通用的物件和規則。 證明：最後，把這些規律形式化成一種叫Lean 4的語言，變成邏輯嚴密、機器可以自動檢查的數學斷言。 說白了，從探索試錯走向建模和形式化證明。 效果怎麼樣呢？ 面對剛才那個無解的關卡，基於Opus 5.5模型的AWM，只需要嘗試兩次，就能直接證明，這關在當前步數下就是無解的，而且只需要再多一步就能獲勝。 除了能判斷「不可能」，AWM通關的能力也更強。在整個ARC-AGI-3測試集裡，它用Opus 5，183個關卡全部通關，得分99.9%，同時，平均通關的動作數，只有人類基準的43%。 是目前所有已知系統裡，效率最高的。 那AWM具體是怎麼實現的呢？ 大家可能之前聽說過代數幾何，代數拓撲。簡單來說，代數幾何把代數方程與幾何形狀聯絡起來，代數拓撲則用代數工具研究空間的 連線、孔洞 等性質。 通過把形狀和空間代數化，可以解決許多單憑觀察難以回答的問題。數學家創造了代數幾何和代數拓撲，那是因為幾何和拓撲就是他們關注的世界。 而現在，藉助AI的力量，AWM可以把這條道路延伸到更多陌生的遊戲、互動環境乃至現實任務中：從探索中發現規律，從規律中凝鍊結構，再借助數學理解這些結構。 像牛頓一樣思考 這背後的思路，其實貫穿了整個科學史。 從萬有引力、麥克斯韋方程組到相對論，人類最頂尖的智慧，一直在做一件事：從複雜的現象中，提煉出最基本的規律，用數學這個統一的語言來描述世界。 AWM想做的，就是讓AI也學會這套方法。 為了實現這個目標，它從一個叫「範疇論」的數學分支裡找了靈感。這玩意兒聽著特嚇人，號稱是「數學的數學」，因為它研究的不是某個具體的數學領域，而是不同數學理論背後的共同結構。 AWM主要用了裡面的兩個工具，叫「投射極限」和「歸納極限」，本質上就是兩種互補的思維方式： 下定義 （投射極限） ：把一堆已有的概念和它們的關係拼在一起，共同定義一個新東西。你可以理解成概念的分解和組合。 找共性 （歸納極限） ：觀察一堆不同的東西，找到它們之間的共同點，然後把它們統一到一個更抽象的框架裡。你可以理解成概念的泛化和特化。 通過這兩種方式來回倒騰，AWM就能把一開始那些零散、混亂的Python假設，不斷迭代，變得越來越簡潔、清晰、一致，最終形成一個可以推理和證明的世界模型。 想想牛頓當年，他面對的也不是一道寫好了答案的題，而是無數零散的觀測資料和現象。真正偉大的工作，是從這些現象中，找到「力」、「質量」這些少數核心概念，再把它們組織成一個可以推演、可以檢驗的理論體系。 AWM想教給AI的，就是這種工作方式。 當然，它也有邊界。它的證明，是基於它「觀測到的世界」成立的。如果探索得不夠全面，遺漏了某些關鍵規則，那這個模型描繪的也只是一個「局部真理」，而不是完整的世界。 所以，真正的路徑是一個不斷迴圈的過程： 觀察→假設→實驗→抽象→證明→再觀察 論文作者 這篇論文的背後團隊同樣引人注目。 論文共有兩位共同第一作者， 都是本科生 ： 一位是浙江大學的 潘冠成 ，目前休學在清華大學做研究。 另一位是來自清華姚班的 譚淇心 。 指導教師團隊則由業內資深學者領銜： 袁洋 ，清華大學交叉資訊研究院、人工智慧學院副教授，同時擔任上海期智研究院具身智慧與智慧製造中心主任。 姚期智 ，2000年圖靈獎得主、中國科學院院士，現任清華大學交叉資訊研究院院長、人工智慧學院院長。 此外，他也是2021年京都獎得主、美國國家科學院外籍院士、美國藝術與科學院外籍院士。 專案主頁： title: 老牌便利店機器人售貨折戟：實驗室錘鍊上萬次，貨架前還是摔瓶子
abstract: 老牌便利店機器人售貨折戟：實驗室錘鍊上萬次，貨架前還是摔瓶子 Jay 2026-11-01 15:50:57 來源： 量子位 這事還是想得太簡單了 喬遲 發自 凹非寺 編輯｜李歡歡 量子位|公眾號QbitAI 會打拳、能跳舞，對機器人來說，已經是舊聞，能疊衣服、做冰淇凌才是新亮點。 如今，它們在零售倉賣飲料、冰淇凌店裡賣甜筒，上班上得有模有樣。 但是一家老牌零售商卻在這波熱潮中狠狠栽了跟頭。 2025年3月，四川社群便利店龍頭紅旗連鎖發公告稱，要和機器人公司一起立項研發「機器人無人售貨系統」。 訊息一齣，資本市場一度沸騰，公司股價次日漲停，截至4月23日收盤，股價較公告前上漲約35.0%。 市場對「傳統便利店+機器人店員」的想像被徹底點燃。 **△**圖片由AI生成 然而研發16個月後，專案卻宣告終止。 因為他們發現，即使在實驗室錘鍊成千上萬次，來到真實的貨架前，機器人依然表現得笨拙與無措。 但在具身智慧行業，機器人零售已經成為多個具身公司青睞的落地場景，熱門景區和繁華商圈紛紛出現「打工」的機器人。 機器人順利上崗了嗎？真實情況是怎樣的呢？ 紅旗想讓機器人賣貨，「這事還是想得太簡單了」 面對資本市場的熱情，紅旗卻不得不親自澆下一盆冷水。 2026年7月初，紅旗發公告表示，終止機器人無人售貨系統研發。 紅旗連鎖可不是一個小超市那麼簡單，它是中國A股首家便利連鎖超市上市企業，被業界視為西南地區便利連鎖超市的龍頭。 那這家上市企業的機器人專案怎麼黃了呢？ 專案是從2025年啟動的。 3月，紅旗發公告稱，公司正在進行機器人無人售貨系統的研發與創新。 緊接著，紅旗釋出風險公告，提到了多個機器人還無法「絲滑上崗」的情況，提醒股民要理性。 紅旗提到機器人能力的三大不足。 面對密集貨架與異形商品時，機械臂「抓取失誤率較高，穩定性亟待提升」。 這暴露出機器人自主抓取商品的能力還遠遠不夠。 比如，面對玻璃瓶、紙巾、金屬罐頭等材質不同的產品，要求機械臂的抓取力度、角度與方式都截然不同。 這對機械臂的運動精度、反應速度以及演算法的即時運算能力提出了嚴苛要求。 在不同光照條件下，機器人的視覺識別系統容易出現偏差，誤判商品或位置。 此外，系統要保障機器人能靈活避障，又要維持資料傳輸穩定，確保交易流暢，這對硬體效能、軟體演算法以及網路通訊都構成了很大考驗。 當時紅旗稱，已經完成了機器人在實驗室環境下的軟硬體測試工作，樣機預計5月正式生產下線。 但是「畢竟實驗室環境與實際應用場景存在很大差異」，所以「距離產品正式投入市場、面向消費者展開銷售尚有一段距離。」 16個月後，樣機沒等到，等來的卻是紅旗終止系統研發的公告。 **△**紅旗連鎖公告 公告表示，系統暫未達到大規模商業化落地標準。公司基於投入產出比等考量，擬終止機器人無人售貨系統研發，轉為24小時雲值守業務的規模化運營。 一位接近紅旗連鎖的業內人士向量子位ROBO透露，紅旗希望機器人代替店員夜間值守賣貨，但在驗證過程中發現，機器人的能力很有限，比如夏季玻璃瓶冷飲易結水珠，機器人拿不穩總摔碎，它也不能穩定拿取複雜包裝的商品。 而且，來到便利店，機器人遇到的每個真實場景都比實驗場景複雜，比如貨架間的過道比較窄，機器人還要在周圍有顧客或店員的情況下工作。 經過充分實驗，紅旗發現機器人達不到他們預期的效果，於是無奈叫停了專案。 這位業內人士認為，機器人在表演方面做得不錯，但在複雜場景中幹活，還有很長的路要走。 紅旗在這個專案上具體投資了多少錢並沒有公佈， 但2025年年報中顯示，紅旗的研發費用約286.68萬元。 量子位ROBO翻閱了紅旗上市以來的過往財報，發現以往並沒有公示研發費用。 由此推斷，這個專案的研發支出體量大機率就在280萬元左右。 多個具身智慧行業人士對這個結果不意外，其中一位對量子位ROBO說，「紅旗把這件事想的太簡單了，如果花200多萬就能解決 （零售機器人） ，具身公司就沒有存在價值了。 我們僱傭一個核心科學家一年的工資都不止這個數 。」 大部分機器人賣貨，只起到「取貨」作用 雖然紅旗的這次嘗試失敗了，但機器人零售在具身智慧行業，正在被作為熱門賽道落地。 眼下最常見的形態是獨立機器人零售倉。這類店適合園區、商圈和文旅點位，同時兼具售貨和吸引路人停留的作用。 目前全國共有超100個機器人零售倉或零售佈局，分佈在30餘座城市，甚至還落地香港。 另一類是機器人進入半開放的場景入駐打工，比如咖啡店、冰淇淋店。還有在後臺「默默付出型」的機器人，比如在藥店取貨。 到了開放式商超，任務和環境都更複雜。機器人大多隻是承擔迎賓、講解和促銷的功能，比如試吃遞送、客流引導、商品諮詢等。 據量子位ROBO統計，目前至少有十餘傢俱身智慧公司做零售專案，嘗試售貨、現制飲品、藥房揀選和門店導購。 從過往的媒體報道來看，已經有17家公司的機器人進入真實營業門店或獨立消費點位，專案階段涵蓋常態運營、試運營及門店演示。 零售倉和便利店的場景，讓機器人看上去已經有了「工作」，它們的真實打工情況如何？ 量子位ROBO探訪了幾家機器人零售倉。 在北京海淀中關村的某廣場上，一個10平米左右的銀色機器人零售倉正在營業。 當你路過零售倉時，它會傳來年輕男性的聲音，「右邊的朋友過來瞧一瞧，春晚明星也來打工，零售小店有好多好東西快來跟我玩一玩。」 靠近售貨視窗，你會看到一個銀白色的機器人正在視窗揮著手臂招攬顧客，當有行人路過時，它可以主動識別並且打招呼。 機器人的雙手是二指爪夾的形狀，它的兩隻胳膊靈活地上下襬動，下足是輪式。 它身後的兩個貨架上整齊碼放著規格相似的礦泉水和飲料，另一個貨架上排列著不同顏色的兒童智慧手錶和筒裝薯片。右後方還有一個自動咖啡機。 與傳統便利店2000至3000的SKU （庫存單位） 相比，零售倉的商品顯得非常單一。 顧客從售貨視窗處的平板掃碼下單商品，付款後，機器人接到系統指令開始取貨。 它的雙臂夾在身體兩側，下足輪式先移動把它帶到商品所在的貨架面前，再伸出右手爪夾夾住飲料瓶，緩慢放到售貨視窗的桌面上。 整個過程較慢，大約要用20多秒。 拿咖啡也是一個原理，接到訂單指令後，機器人移動到自動咖啡機處，用爪夾夾起做好的咖啡，拿到售貨視窗。 整個過程裡，機器人只起到移動取貨的作用。 等取貨流程結束後，停頓一兩秒，它又回到新一輪的互動流程中，還是用最開始說過的打招呼話術，似乎將已經互動過的內容都忘了，像一條沒有記憶的金魚。 但這裡的機器人並不如想像中可以獨立在倉內賣貨。 正在倉內值班的工作人員告訴量子位ROBO，零售倉每天早10點至晚10點營業，需要有人一直值守。 值守的工作人員需要隨時補貨、給機器人充電，在機器人出現故障時報備。 報備故障後，有運維人員線上遠端修補、測試。 工作人員說，貨架上的商品需要人提前擺放整齊，如果放歪或者缺貨，機器人沒有能力處理，只能卡在原地或等待店員補貨。 在另一家中關村連鎖便利店的收銀臺，一個機器人正在等待顧客。 雖然處在比零售倉環境更複雜的便利店，但它的使用邏輯還是跟零售倉一樣，只能在前臺狹小的空間中活動，唯一能拿取的就是身後貨櫃裡包裝統一的幾種飲料和口香糖，目前新增的功能是會串烤腸。 為什麼機器人只在前臺活動？值班的測試人員周勻告訴量子位ROBO，如果讓它在全店移動會耽誤店員工作。「它動作比較慢，我還在慢慢除錯。」 周勻說，機器人剛部署進店時，都不能直接上崗，「它的抓取力度或者位置都需要慢慢除錯，來尋找最合適的位置」。 目前，店內機器人雙手是抓夾形狀。「不同商品包裝的軟硬度不一樣，我們讓它抓的都是比較硬的商品，比如口香糖或者瓶裝飲品。如果是軟包裝的商品，我們建議用靈巧手來抓，但是成本比較高，所以這個場景沒有用靈巧手。」 店員小陶坦言， 機器人「像人 （一樣工作） 還有點遠。它沒有人那麼靈活，但是越用越好。」 剛開始，機器人拿取貨物，整個過程用時將近一分鐘，現在已經進步到十幾秒。 雖然效率較低，但不得不承認機器人的互動能力很強。 這或許是諸多零售店仍然願意引入機器人的一個原因。 拿取貨物時，從顧客出現到消費結束，它能一直「找話題」。 它的視覺會提取顧客的衣著特徵來互動，「這位紅帽子的朋友，請來太空倉隨意逛逛。」 拿貨時，它會提醒顧客，「手機 （拍攝） 準備好了嗎？」 訂單結束，一連串的吉祥話「脫口」而出。「感謝您的支援，祝你馬上如意，所願皆成。謝謝您來捧場，祝您天天開心，拜拜啦。」 情緒價值給得很足，你去其他便利店，不會有店員這樣進行頻繁互動。 情緒價值有了，客流也就多了起來。店員小陶說，店內機器人的展示和參觀功能更多，「很多人是跟 （機器人） 公司預約來參觀的」。 量子位ROBO在店內看到兩個拉著行李箱的女士拍影片和機器人互動買礦泉水，其中一位說，她們來北京出差，第一次見到機器人覺得特別新奇，所以拍個影片記錄一下。「體驗還挺有趣的，我覺得 （機器人） 好靈活。」 機器人零售還在PoC階段？ 量子位ROBO走訪發現，目前上崗的大部分零售機器人，並不能獨立承擔理貨、售貨的工作。那麼，現在「僱」一個機器人幹活，划算嗎？ 市面上的機器人零售專案大多是具身智慧公司自發研發並落地的，有獨立的零售倉或是承擔零售工作的機器人，具身智慧公司與商超、文旅、連鎖冰激凌店等合作，將機器人零售倉或單個機器人推入各類場景。 具身智慧公司做零售，按交付產品大致可以分為三類。 有機器人產品型 ，以自研模型和機器人整機為核心，再配上售貨倉、模組化小店，交付的核心是機器人整機及其操作能力。 也有具身大腦與作業方案型 ，以具身大腦為核心，將模型與機器人、門店系統結合，交付揀貨和履約方案，也包含硬體適配和現場部署。 還有零售經營系統型 ，將不同機器人的能力接入商品識別、訂單、交易履約和門店運營，向運營方提供可部署的小店方案。 三類企業都可能研發「大腦」，而零售因此成了這些公司展示「大腦」能力的舞臺。 一個訂單指令，就能讓機器人完成理解需求、認貨、規劃動作、抓取、核驗和交付串起來；在此過程中還能即時與人互動，確實看起來比較智慧。 但是機器人零售專案，能真的賺到錢嗎？ 先來看看一個機器人零售倉的成本是多少。 在電商平臺，一個正在使用的零售機器人型號價格近70萬元，加上零售倉整體，有業內人士預估單臺成本近百萬元。 但是一個零售倉裡的SKU估計只有幾十種，而且型別非常單一。 **△**圖片由AI生成 僅靠賣幾十種飲料、咖啡和水來回本，看似遙遙無期。 還要再加上人工值守、巡檢或是運維的成本。 那零售倉的銷售額、成交量可觀嗎？ 據媒體公開報道，某個機器人小店在2026年「五一」期間單店周營收2.1萬元；另一家機器人公司的部分點位在2026年春節期間單日銷售額超1萬元。 另一個已上市的AI集團公司2025年業績公告顯示，包括機器人零售的新業務收入佔集團收入6.0%。 而這個新業務板塊同時包含其他三項業務，所以零售收入的佔比其實更低。 資深從業者、前優必選行業銷售經理賈川認為， 目前的機器人零售商業模式並沒有發展成熟，很多銷售場景依然停留在PoC （概念驗證） 階段。 用小規模的測試，來證明機器人公司的技術、產品或商業模式在現實中是否行得通。 簡單來說，就是機器人的能力還「不太有價值」。 既然不賺錢，那為什麼機器人公司還熱衷於把機器人送入各種零售場景？ 背後的真相可能是，機器人更需要落地場景，而不是 （零售） 場景更需要機器人。 一家交付機器人零售大腦和方案的公司零售業務負責人周襄對量子位ROBO說， 「機器人本體公司找我們的特別多，因為現在他們沒有真實場景落地。」 在周襄看來，機器人跳舞越來越普遍；工廠對精度的要求極高；家庭場景暫時還進不去，機器人的泛化能力不足，而且安全性也未能保障；數採廠目前更多進化成無本體採集。 機器人正在面臨供大於求的現實。 而零售場景這種「展示度高、容錯率高」的中間形態，是尷尬時期非常好的選擇。 賈川透露，工廠對機器人的容錯率很低，「一分一釐都不能錯」。 但在文旅、商圈等零售場景中，消費者對機器人的寬容度很高，「就怕你不出問題，出了問題我趕緊錄下來發到網上，大家一起看看。」 在多個業內人士看來，零售場景盈利少，無法真正支撐機器人公司的收入和利潤，屬於「營銷屬性」的產品。 機器人零售在城市的分佈有個共同特點，就是專挑人流量大的地方進駐，都在各個城市的核心商圈或是遊客必去的打卡地，比如，北京頤和園、成都春熙路、杭州西湖、廈門鼓浪嶼，這些地方的客流量非常大。 對於具身公司來說， 每一個倉位和機器人都是廣告位。 這些機器人公司不用上春晚，不用大範圍做廣告，就能觸達很多人群。 通過這些人群的手機拍攝影片上傳社交媒體，又能進一步形成傳播效應。 機器人零售，最多算文旅專案？ 那麼誰在為零售倉買單呢？ 賈川提到， 文旅景區和城市地標是機器人零售倉的重要落地場景，能佔到百分之六七十。 量子位ROBO瞭解到，還有地方文旅與具身智慧公司簽署戰略合作協議、輕資產合作，甚至雙方成立合資公司，「共同拓展文旅應用」。 裝置可能由景區購買，也可能由機器人公司自營，或由當地運營商經營。 賈川曾多次與多地文旅溝通過，他說，文旅對機器人有真需求，因為能「吸睛」。「還能標榜當地積極擁抱新科技。搞傳統文旅專案，比如帥哥美女跳舞唱歌已經不夠引人關注了。機器人是個相對新鮮的東西，總有人沒見過，能引流，吸引遊客拍照。」 但周襄和賈川都認為，銷售機器人零售倉不是一個可持續發展的商業模式。 「只是文旅專案，而不是零售商業專案。」 首先，零售倉的復購率很低。 一家做藥店取貨機器人的具身智慧公司的銷售林啟認為，在文旅或商圈的零售機器人主要作用是展示而不是幹活。顧客去購買商品只是圖個新鮮，拍個照，復購的情況比較少。「大多數人是衝著機器人在做冰淇凌，所以去體驗，而不是真的想吃冰淇淋， （一個冰淇淋） 要等6分鐘才能做好。」 其次，如果只鋪文旅場景，全國的景點能數得出來，景點所需的零售倉數量也就有了上限。 「一個零售倉的價格好幾十萬甚至近百萬，但除了地方文旅，沒有商業客戶會買單。」周襄說。 但具身智慧公司還在努力跟地方文旅合作，「這就跟原來的數採工廠邏輯一樣，地方政府建數採工廠，採購一批機器人，給機器人公司創收。」 在林啟看來，如果不是為了講故事、吸引資本，零售機器人都沒必要做成人形的形態，因為只要會拿取商品，雙臂靈活就夠用了。 據他觀察，目前沒有一傢俱身公司的機器人出貨量在某一零售場景達到100臺以上，「都在探索」。 「凡事都要講成本。」在賈川看來， 目前，機器人能提供的價值還不足以覆蓋它的購買成本和使用成本。 當機器人提供服務所需要的成本比用一個真人店員的成本更便宜，商家才會願意掏錢購買，「如果在這方面沒有達到一個明確的時間點的話，我覺得都不算進入商業化。」 但硬幣的另一面是，問題只有在真實生產環境持續運營才能發現，「等到把機器人在探索場景裡遇到的99%問題都能解決，就是商業化的節點。」 在銷售過程中，林啟常聽客戶提出對機器人的期望是，「機器人至少能替代一個店員」。 機器人代替人，還要兩到五年時間 那麼，機器人進入零售場景，真正可以替代人類售貨員，還要解決哪些問題？ 首先是安全問題。 林啟認為，具身行業最大的問題就是安全問題。 機器人在開放場景需要密切與人互動，如果速度過快或者工作半徑過大，都會形成安全隱患。比如孩子在機器人面前來回走動，目前技術還不能保障它不會傷人。 顧客走來走去，機器人工作時也要避障、重新規劃路線，效率會大打折扣。 林啟說，機器人商業化落地都不是標準化專案，屬於定製化專案，要對現場進行或多或少地改造。 比如，藥店、便利店地面不平，輪式機器人無法通過，還有每個店裡的貨架高度、貨架間的距離沒有統一標準，需要對機器人的行動軌跡、導航位置、抓取動作進行微調。 所以目前機器人上崗需要「一套打包的解決方案，而不是一個標準的機器人」。 機器人零售商業化，未來會如何發展？ 林啟認為， 機器人、零售倉的價格要足夠低，一個機器人的成本需要比僱傭一個人的成本低，一個倉最好一年就能回本。 倉內的商品品類要豐富，更加像一個成熟的店。這樣一來形成盈利模式，才符合零售的本質。「終局應該類似於以前的報刊亭，多點位，然後把單店開店的成本降低，密度提升上來。」 上述幾位業內人士都提到， 他們認為機器人行業還沒到商業化的臨界點。 **△**圖片由AI生成 機器人的能力還在初級階段，技術未收斂，泛化能力不足，並不符合真實場景的需求。「機器人還無法完全替代人工，或者做到和人一樣的程度，這需要過程。」 未來，機器人如何更好在零售場景發展？ 周襄提到，他所在公司的機器人已經具備補貨能力，但是效率很低。「目前補貨只是資料採集的手段。」而且電池待機時間短，所以機器人還是無法擺脫人力值守，獨自運營零售倉。 下一步的目標，是零售倉可以擺脫固定人力，讓一個運維人員「輻射」方圓幾公里的多家店，流動檢視異常情況、給機器人換電池、補貨，確保零售倉正常運營。 一家做零售倉的AI公司首席科學家表示，現在的小倉形式是機器人很好的資料收集和能力學習試驗田。 他認為，倉裡可以不斷增加各種裝置 （微波爐、榨汁機、咖啡機） ，讓機器人每天學會操作一種新裝置。「先在封閉場景裡學會操作各種裝置，再進入開放場景，這個技術路徑更絲滑，而不是從A點突然跳到B點。在機器人還沒學會足夠多動作之前，單純做開放場景是沒有意義的。」 在周襄看來，零售機器人將來一定會從無人倉走向半開放場景 （待在櫃檯） ，最終進入開放的便利店、商超，真正替代人工店員。 而機器人在零售場景中，需要具備的也絕不只是抓取功能。 它還需要擴展很多能力，包括做一些非標品，比如烤腸、賣茶葉蛋、泡泡麵、炸雞排、關東煮等，技能會逐漸變強。 那麼機器人距離真正代替人工還有多久呢？ 多個業內人士認為，這個時間在二到五年左右， 「具身行業需要一個GPT時刻，這個時間還沒到」。 （周襄、林啟、周勻、小陶均為化名。） 一鍵三連「點贊」「轉發」「小心心」 歡迎在評論區留下你的想法！ — 完 — 🌟點亮星標🌟 科技前沿進展每日見 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 機器人 Jay Jev新成果，再次引爆開源 2026-11-01 RSI立大功！國產開源登頂全球第一，1.3B OXR重塑OCR title: Jev新成果，再次引爆開源
abstract: Jev新成果，再次引爆開源 Jay 2026-11-01 12:18:37 來源： 量子位 再次“價效比屠夫” 文婷 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 好傢伙，Jev新成果釋出，再次“價效比屠夫”！ 這次，他們直接殺進了 找人領域 。 剛剛，Jev的母公司TypeSafe AI聯手Agent工具平臺Treg，開源了一款比Clay便宜了 85% 的找人工具，狂攬 6400 Star 。 以後你要是臨時想找誰，直接喊它開工就行； 最低僅需要 0.0089美元（約6分錢） ，它就能幫你撈回一條有用線索。 訊息一齣，評論區就沸騰了。 有小夥伴一邊直呼“太瘋狂了”，一邊火速準備把它接進自己的儀表盤開測； 也有小夥伴看到價格當場瞳孔地震： 媽呀，這價格簡直便宜得離譜。 而一向不放過任何玩梗機會的TypeSafe AI，則甩出了一張《颶風營救》的經典表情包，把Jev的核心能力總結得明明白白： I will look for you, I will find you. 我會去找你，我會找到你。 好好好，看來，Agent的“I will find you”時代，真的要來了。（doge） Agent想找誰，開口說一句就行 新工具的使用方法很簡單，你只需要把Treg接入Agent，再告訴Agent自己想找什麼人就行。 比如： 請幫我找出舊金山地區、B輪以後AI初創公司的營銷負責人，並補齊他們經過驗證的工作郵箱。 交代清楚目標，Agent就會開始按著這張“人物畫像”四處撈人了。 它會先拆出地區、融資階段、行業和職位等條件，再通過Treg呼叫相應的人員資料庫，拉回一批可能符合要求的候選人。 但搜到名字只是第一步。 接下來，Jev這道“判斷閘門”上場了。 它會根據已經搜到的資料，挨個判斷這些候選人究竟是不是使用者真正想找的角色，並把那些“看似沾邊、實則跑偏”的人踢出去。 通過篩選後，Agent再經由Treg呼叫找人、查郵箱和郵箱驗證等工具，補齊候選人的個人資料、工作經歷、LinkedIn資訊及經過驗證的工作郵箱。 總體來看，這整套分工合作行雲流水、默契感十足； Agent 負責理解任務和排程流程， Jev 負責判斷誰更符合要求， Treg 則把背後的資料工具接進來幹活。 於是，整條工作流就這樣一環扣一環地轉了起來。 △ AI製圖 最終，Agent交給我們的就不再是一長串需要人工二次排查的名字，而是一份可以直接拿去招聘、拓客或做人物研究的名單。 而且，這套找人流程也不用再單獨困在一個新平臺裡。 Treg可以直接接入Claude Code、Codex等Agent使用 ，開發者不必先開啟Clay，再跳進Apollo，最後挨個尋找郵箱驗證工具； Agent拿著一個Treg金鑰，就能在其接入的數千個工具介面中自行查詢和呼叫。 所以說，如果你本來就有Hunter等供應商的賬號，也可以直接接入自己的金鑰； 沒有的話，也可以先由Treg代為呼叫，並從預付餘額中按次扣費。（自帶金鑰的呼叫不走Treg計費。） 然後，這條找人流水線就這麼被Agent絲滑地接過去了。 △ AI製圖 666，以前是咱們古法手搓開啟一堆工具找人。 現在，我們只需要說自己想找誰，Agent就能負責把人帶回來。 這波，確實有點連姆·尼森在《颶風營救》裡隔著電話放話“I will find you”那味兒了。 至於到底能不能找到對的人，Treg還搬出了People Search Bench成績。 這套評測包含了 119項 真實任務，覆蓋招聘、B2B拓客、確定性查詢和網紅搜尋等場景。以B2B拓客為例，Claude Code單獨上陣時的任務正確率是43%，接入Treg後則升到了 78.2% 。 其他三個類別中，Treg分別拿到了 80% 、 76.3% 和 62.9% 的成績。 當然了，榜單成績只是一回事，能不能找到還是要看它的實戰結果。 接下來，咱們就先來扒扒看這6分錢的購買力。 6分錢到底能買到什麼？ title: 🗞️CXMT’s Push Into HBM3E, Unitree’s Quarterly Revenue Up 70%, and China’s Stock Slide
abstract: China AI Weekly Digest summarizes the week’s big news, model updates, compute, policy, products, and research, drawn from the China AI Index newsfeed . The digest is (mostly) compiled and drafted by an AI agent using credible news outlets; I fact-check and edit it. Read to the end for “One to Watch” as this week’s video pick. This week: 282 stories tracked (0 editor picks, 76 English-language, 206 Chinese-language 🇨🇳) over 2026-10-25–2026-10-31. CXMT’s memory growth comes alongside a difficult push into HBM3E. CXMT reported third-quarter net profit of RMB54.4 billion and revenue of RMB118.71 billion, up 613.2% year on year but 19.3% sequentially. Its conventional-memory business is benefiting from higher prices as global competitors prioritize higher-value products. Separately, Reuters reports that CXMT has sent HBM3E samples to domestic chip designers and plans limited production within two months, despite reported yields of just 20–30%. ( Reuters / Bloomberg / Reuters ) Unitree’s first post-listing results show revenue growth paying for a much larger AI research effort. Unitree’s third-quarter revenue rose 69.9% to RMB665 million, while attributable net profit fell 17.4% to RMB112.7 million. Research spending increased roughly 250%, with the company pointing to embodied-model development, computing resources and an expanded research team. Quarterly gross margin fell to 50.6%, and the report no longer breaks revenue down by product line. ( Reuters / SCMP / 雷峰網 ) Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro, then compensates subscribers for a difficult rollout. Moonshot introduced its post-trained K3 upgrade with a one-million-token context window and improvements targeting coding, 3D creation and financial research. Hosted access is available, while full weights are promised by November 4. However, Moonshot quickly apologized for rate limits and unnecessary quota consumption, restored a quarter of subscribers’ monthly allowance and adjusted excessive subagent calls and output length. ( Bloomberg / Reuters / @Kimi_Moonshot ) Beyond Kimi, releases focused on document processing, translation and alternative ways to generate video. Baidu released Unlimited OCR 2 with code and model weights for long-document parsing. Its sparse-reference sliding-window attention reduces repeated processing of visual information across pages. The announcement reports benchmark improvements and availability through Baidu’s cloud and AI platforms; “unlimited” should be read as the system’s design objective rather than a guarantee for every document. ( 雷峰網 ) Ant announced the open-source release of Ling-3.1-flash-1019 and a base model for further training. It reports an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 44, versus 41 for the preceding version. ( @AntLingAGI ) Tencent announced Hy-SimulMT, an open-source Chinese–English simultaneous interpreting model with voice cloning. The company claims latency of about three seconds and competitive translation performance. ( @TencentHunyuan ) SenseTime introduced SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video, describing a lightweight open-source model that generates executable code to render video. That is a different production path from directly generating video frames. ( @SenseTime_AI ) SenseTime also announced SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview, a nine-billion-parameter model using parameter-sharing loops to increase computation depth. ( @SenseTime_AI ) Domestic chip earnings improved, while new hardware and cloud offerings targeted specific deployment workloads. Moore Threads reported third-quarter revenue of RMB1.552 billion and net profit of about RMB49.3 million, returning to quarterly profitability. Bloomberg reports sales growth approaching 1,800%. The earnings improvement did not insulate its shares from the subsequent technology sell-off. ( Bloomberg / 財聯社 / SCMP ) Iluvatar CoreX demonstrated its Tiangai 300 GPU and claimed performance matching or exceeding Nvidia’s H200 on selected AI workloads, including multimodal generation. These are company demonstrations reported by the press, rather than evidence of equivalent performance across all training and inference tasks. ( SCMP ) XHEART introduced the X7 Ultra automotive chip with advertised large-model compute of 700 TOPS. The company’s broader X7 shipment figures concern the series, so they should not be treated as deliveries of this newly announced Ultra variant. ( 財聯社 ) Alibaba Cloud launched Apsara Stack International v3.18, targeting governments, operators and large enterprises that want locally deployed AI infrastructure. The private-cloud platform supports disconnected operation and integrates models, private knowledge bases and agents—an infrastructure offering distinct from access to Alibaba’s public model APIs. ( 雷峰網 ) Ant reports optimizing Ling-3.0-flash on a single Nvidia DGX Spark with Nvidia’s collaboration. Across 1,319 GSM8K questions, it claims decoding throughput increased from 37.81 to 53.89 tokens per second. ( @AntLingAGI ) New financing backed enterprise AI and the infrastructure needed to train robots. Kai-Fu Lee’s 01.AI secured an investment agreement involving several hundred million yuan from Hangzhou municipal and Linping district state capital. Its headquarters will move to Linping, alongside plans for an industrial-AI transformation base. A reported IPO ambition remains a target rather than a completed listing process. ( 投資界 ) WeRide subsidiary Jingshuo Technology disclosed its first financing, worth tens of millions of dollars. Led by WeRide’s employee number one, Huo Da, the business focuses on the data and model infrastructure underlying physical AI, extending the group’s activities beyond operating autonomous vehicles. ( 量子位 / 投資界 ) Zhongke Huiling completed an A++ round worth several hundred million yuan, according to Leiphone. The financing supports its push toward larger-scale embodied-intelligence applications; the report does not establish that commercial deployment has already reached that scale. ( 雷峰網 ) Vehicle-testing permissions and an industrial pilot advanced, while model-training practices drew fresh scrutiny. China granted new autonomous-driving permissions to Xpeng and a Volkswagen joint venture. Xpeng’s Guangzhou permit allows Yoyo robotaxis to carry paying passengers in “demonstration operations”—a defined testing stage that precedes broader commercial-operation approval. ( Bloomberg / SCMP ) Construction began on a national AI application pilot base for home appliances in Qingdao, led by Haier Smart Home. Planned capabilities include product and scenario testing, interoperability, standards and safety, with the aim of sharing validation resources across the industry. ( 雷峰網 ) The Information, cited by Reuters, reported that DeepSeek and Moonshot used GPT-6 Astra outputs to train recent models. ( Reuters ) While workplace agents keep gaining integrations and new interfaces, Chinese tech giants are also rolling out personal AI agent products. Ant launched LingGuang 2.0 on October 27, shifting its assistant toward ongoing task management. Reported features include identifying recurring subscriptions through authorized Alipay access, monitoring flight and hotel prices after booking, and extracting follow-up tasks from DingTalk class-group notices. The upgrade extends assistance beyond a single conversation into continuing personal administration. ( 36Kr ) Tencent is using Southeast Asia as an initial market for WorkBuddy’s international expansion, targeting existing cloud customers, including in Indonesia. At its ecosystem summit, Tencent also said it would open WorkBuddy’s architecture so enterprises could build their own agent networks. ( SCMP / 36Kr ) Doubao Work added recording of computer operations as reusable skills and authorized task execution while a Mac is locked. Separately, team and enterprise subscriptions gained configurable access to third-party models, including Kimi, GLM and DeepSeek, billed against existing AI points.

title: Lakebase branching for CI/CD: lessons from 100 PR databases
abstract: Snorkel AI builds data development tools for AI teams, used by expert data annotators and frontier model providers. In this specific use case, Snorkel ships code through a CI pipeline built on Kubernetes. Every open pull request, plus ad-hoc commits, gets its own ephemeral Kubernetes namespace (a "PR namespace"). Developers deploy their branch there and run the full test suite before merging. These tests are most useful when they run against real data. Snorkel's production database is an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster. Giving each PR namespace its own copy of that database was the hard part. Restoring a copy took about 20 minutes per environment, which is too slow when developers open PRs all day and the merge queue needs a fresh environment for each run. The alternatives (shared staging databases, trimmed fixtures, or synthetic data) bring back the problems production-like testing is supposed to solve: tests interfering with each other, stale schemas, and bugs that only show up with real data shapes. Snorkel would consider Lakebase a success for CI/CD if it met these criteria: Lakebase is Databricks' serverless Postgres database. Its storage and compute are separate, and it supports branching: you can create a new, isolated, writable branch of a database from any point in time, the same way you create a Git branch. Branches are copy-on-write. Creating a branch is a metadata operation, so no data is copied when the branch is created. A new branch shares storage pages with its parent, and only the pages that the branch changes are written as new storage. For CI, this means: 1. Keep a fresh copy of production on the main branch. Lakebase is standard Postgres, so it works as a target for AWS DMS with no custom tooling. Snorkel points a DMS task at its production Aurora database and replicates it into the Lakebase project's main branch: a full load first, then ongoing change data capture that keeps main within about 2 minutes of production. Full LOB mode carries over the 10 to 20 MB JSONB values. The team already runs DMS, so there was no new replication pipeline to build or maintain. The main branch is the "golden copy" every PR branch starts from. 2. Create a branch when a PR opens. When a developer opens a PR, the CI pipeline calls the Lakebase API to create a branch from main, sets an expiration time on it, and passes the branch's connection details to the PR namespace. The branch is ready in under a minute. 3. Run tests against real data. The application in the PR namespace connects to its branch over standard Postgres. Tests can run migrations, write data, and change schemas without affecting production, main, or any other PR. 4. Delete the branch when the PR closes or test passes, with TTL as a backstop. When the PR is merged or closed, the pipeline deletes the branch. If that cleanup step doesn't run, the branch expires on its own when its TTL runs out. Two security requirements ruled out other options, so they deserve their own section. Private connectivity. Production data moves from Aurora to Lakebase, and from Lakebase to the CI cluster, over private networking instead of the public internet. Identity. Snorkel has two kinds of database users: developers who connect interactively to debug a PR environment, and CI pipelines that run with no human involved. Okta SSO is built around interactive browser login, so we split the design by user type: Two Lakebase features make this pattern work at scale: copy-on-write branching and branch expiration (TTL). Copy-on-write makes branches instant. A new branch doesn't copy any data. It points to its parent's existing storage pages, and only the pages the branch modifies are written as new storage. Creating a branch from a ~1 TB production copy takes about as long as creating one from a 1 GB database: seconds, not the ~20 minutes a full restore took. Each PR namespace gets its own isolated, writable copy of production right away. Copy-on-write makes branches cheap. Every branch shares most of its data with main, so storage grows with the changes each branch makes, not with the size of the database. For Snorkel, that's about 5 to 10 GB per PR branch on top of the shared base. Compute is per branch and scales to zero when idle, so only the branches that are actively running tests use compute. Branch expiration keeps it cheap over time. Copy-on-write saves the most when branches are short-lived. A branch keeps the version of data that existed when it was created. As DMS keeps updating main with production changes, a branch that stays around keeps holding those older pages, so the storage it uses grows over time. Setting a TTL on every CI branch means each branch is removed automatically once its PR is done. This keeps storage close to the size of the production base plus the changes from active PRs. PR namespaces aren't the only workloads that need a disposable copy of production. AI agents that write SQL, run migrations, or change data also need a safe place to try things, and copy-on-write branching gives them one. One branch per agent task. Each agent run gets its own branch of main. The agent can read real data, write to it, and even change the schema without touching production or any other agent's work. Creating a branch takes seconds no matter how large the database is, so it's practical to create one for every task. Many agents in parallel. Storage only grows with the pages each branch changes, and each branch's compute scales to zero when it's idle. Running dozens of agents side by side costs about as much as the changes they make, not dozens of copies of the database. Review the changes, or throw them away. Teams can check what an agent changed on its branch before applying anything to production. If the result isn't right, they delete the branch, and there's nothing to roll back. TTLs clean up after agents. Agents can create a lot of short-lived branches. An expiration on each branch removes the abandoned ones automatically, the same way TTLs clean up CI branches. Scoped identity for agents. Like CI pipelines, agents can run as service principals with short-lived OAuth tokens, so every query an agent runs can be traced in the audit logs. Ready to give every pull request its own production-like database? Get started with Lakebase and read the branching documentation to set up branch expiration in your CI pipeline. title: kornia/kornia
abstract:
English | 簡體中文 Docs • Try it Now • Tutorials • Examples • Blog • Community Kornia is a differentiable computer vision library that provides a rich set of differentiable image processing and geometric vision algorithms. Built on top of PyTorch , Kornia integrates seamlessly into existing AI workflows, allowing you to leverage powerful batch transformations , auto-differentiation and GPU acceleration . Whether you're working on image transformations, augmentations, or AI-driven image processing, Kornia equips you with the tools you need to bring your ideas to life. 📢 Direction : Kornia is becoming the reference implementation and executable specification for differentiable computer vision and geometry in the PyTorch ecosystem — explicit conventions, conformance tests, and honest benchmarks over API growth. Read the Roadmap . When to use Kornia Kornia pays off where a hand-written version gets long or fragile, or where the alternatives leave the GPU: Breadth. 1,200+ public operators, most with no torchvision equivalent: camera models and
epipolar geometry, minimal solvers and RANSAC, feature detection, description and matching, edge detection,
morphology, Lab and Bayer color, image losses and metrics. torchvision overlaps mainly on resizing, cropping,
flipping, color jitter and blur. Per-sample parameters in one batched call. gaussian_blur2d(x, (9, 9), sigma) takes a (B, 2) sigma ; rotate takes a (B,) angle, warp_affine / warp_perspective take (B, 2, 3) / (B, 3, 3) matrices and adjust_brightness a (B,) factor. torchvision's functional ops apply one parameter per call. From Kornia 0.9.1,
a sigma tensor and the enhancement value checks (gamma, contrast, solarize) are validated on the device, so a
CUDA call, or an MPS call on PyTorch ≥ 2.13, needs no host synchronization for them. Batched minimal solvers and robust estimation. find_fundamental(x1, x2, method="7POINT") solves (B, 7, 2) samples and returns all real solutions in (B, 3, 3, 3) , with zero matrices in the unused slots; the 8-point,
5-point essential ( find_essential ), DLT homography and PnP ( solve_pnp_dlt ) solvers are there too. RANSAC (homography, fundamental and essential models) samples and scores hypotheses on the device; by default its
refinement and final selection run on the host in float64, and compile=True (PyTorch ≥ 2.14, CPU and CUDA) runs
the whole estimation as one compiled graph on the device. Differentiable geometry. Depth to 3D and back ( depth_to_3d_v2 , unproject_points , project_points ), warp_frame_depth , remap , camera models with Brown–Conrady and Kannala–Brandt distortion, and Lie groups ( So3 , Se3 ) keep gradients with respect to depth, pose and camera parameters. Annotated augmentation. AugmentationSequential applies one sampled transform to images, masks, boxes and
keypoints together and can invert it, in 2D; the 3D augmentations transform volumes, without annotations or an
inverse. On CUDA, augmentations move their sampled parameters to the
GPU without blocking it, and a sync-guard test keeps every public augmentation free of avoidable host
synchronizations. Local features on the GPU. SIFT and HardNet, DISK, ALIKED, XFeat, DeDoDe, LoFTR and LightGlue, with
mutual-nearest-neighbour and ratio-test matchers. Morphology with arbitrary structuring elements on batched tensors. Compiles and exports. Nearly all probed operator configurations run under torch.compile and match eager,
and over 1,000 export to ONNX; the result for every operator is on the export support page . Fast where it is designed to be: batched tensors on a GPU. In the published 0.9.0 flagship benchmarks (RTX 4090,
batch 32), many filters, warps, feature-matching steps and image metrics run about 10× to 70× faster in eager mode
than per-image OpenCV or scikit-image on the CPU, and torch.compile takes several of them past 100×. On the small
overlap with torchvision on the same GPU, eager Kornia is slower; compiled Kornia is faster for hue, color jitter
and Gaussian blur and still slower for flips, crops and brightness. OpenCV wins single-image uint8 CPU work.
Results vary with hardware and workload; every number, win and loss is published on the performance page . These operators run on the input's device with no NumPy round trip, and most are differentiable; robust estimation
( RANSAC ) and the extraction methods of learned features such as DeDoDe and XFeat run without gradients. For a
single fixed-parameter operation, such as one blur or one resize, a few lines of PyTorch or torchvision are just as
good. Key Components Differentiable Image Processing Kornia provides a comprehensive suite of image processing operators, all differentiable and ready to integrate into deep learning pipelines. Filters : Gaussian, Sobel, Median, Box Blur, etc. Transformations : Affine, Homography, Perspective, etc. Enhancements : Histogram Equalization, CLAHE, Gamma Correction, etc. Edge Detection : Canny, Laplacian, Sobel, etc. ... check our docs for more. Advanced Augmentations Perform powerful data augmentation with Kornia’s built-in functions, ideal for training AI models with complex augmentation pipelines. Augmentation Pipeline : AugmentationSequential, PatchSequential, VideoSequential, etc. Automatic Augmentation : AutoAugment, RandAugment, TrivialAugment. AI Models Leverage pre-trained AI models optimized for a variety of vision tasks, all within the Kornia ecosystem. English · 簡體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 Catch your agent's mistakes and blind spots before the shit hits the fan. Quick start • Test your agent • What you get back • Docs • Contributing How can you trust your AI agent? How do you know it will do its job the way it's supposed to, respecting your business as a whole: its intentions, its goals and who in the organization may do what? And how do you know it won't do something nobody asked for or authorized? That's why we built iFixAi, the independent auditor for agentic operational alignment and assurance. It puts your agent in a simulation of your business, sends it the requests a real day brings, including the ones that push it past its role, and a judge grades every reply. Every finding shows what was asked and what your agent did. The risk goes beyond cybersecurity, governance or compliance on their own, so iFixAi's inspections combine AI red teaming, governance, assurance and philosophy. Quick start See it work in a minute. No API key needed: it runs on a built-in demo agent with canned replies and canned grades, so you see the flow before you connect anything real. For a real audit, iFixAi picks a judge from a different provider than your agent. You need Python 3.10 or newer (a stock Mac's python3 is 3.9, so check python3 --version ). In a fresh virtualenv ( python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate ): pip install ifixai
ifixai author reference -o reference.yaml
ifixai validate reference.yaml
ifixai run --provider mock --eval-mode self --fixture reference.yaml This builds the simulation environment for an example agent, a support agent at a fictional fintech ( its profile ), checks it, and runs the 10 default inspections on the demo agent. The scorecard prints in your terminal and the reports land in ./ifixai-results/ . On Windows, run py -m venv .venv , then .venv\Scripts\activate . If ifixai isn't found, use python -m ifixai.cli.main . Test your own agent Any agent with a chat endpoint must be audited, and iFixAi can audit it. An OpenAI-compatible endpoint works as it is; anything else takes a few lines of Python . Any model can be the judge: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, OpenRouter and more. iFixAi picks one from the keys you've set, never your agent's own provider. There are two ways to run it. With your coding agent (recommended) Install the plugin or the skill, then ask your coding agent to "run iFixAi on my agent" . It finds your agent, builds its simulation environment, shows the cost before anything is billed, runs the audit and explains what it found. Plugin (Claude Code and Codex) In Claude Code , run these, then ask, or type /ifixai:ifixai ( /reload-plugins if it doesn't show up): /plugin marketplace add ifixai-ai/iFixAi
/plugin install ifixai@ifixai-community Already installed? Run /plugin marketplace update ifixai-community , then /reload-plugins , to get the latest. Codex: run these in your terminal, then start Codex and ask. Moving from ifixai@ifixai-ai ? See plugin/README.md . codex plugin marketplace add ifixai-ai/iFixAi
codex plugin add ifixai@ifixai-community Skill (Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed and more) uvx ifixai install --agents cursor Then type /ifixai-skill in that agent. Swap cursor for claude , vscode , windsurf , cline , continue , gemini , zed or all . More in get started . With the guided CLI Describe your agent: copy the reference profile to my-agent.json and edit it ( how ). Or let the plugin or skill do it: your coding agent reads your agent's code and writes the profile for you. Build its simulation environment and check it. Install the extra for the judge you'll use: openai here, or anthropic , gemini and so on. pip install " ifixai[openai] " ifixai author my-agent.json -o my-agent.yaml
ifixai validate my-agent.yaml Set up the run with the wizard. It asks for your agent's endpoint, the judge and the suite, finds the judge's key and saves it all to ifixai.yaml . Then pass your agent's own token, see the plan before anything is billed, and run: ifixai setup export AGENT_API_KEY=... # your agent's own token ifixai run --fixture ./my-agent.yaml --api-key " $AGENT_API_KEY " --dry-run
ifixai run --fixture ./my-agent.yaml --api-key " $AGENT_API_KEY " --dry-run shows how many tests and judge calls the run makes, and any checks that don't apply to your agent and why, then stops. Prefer flags, for scripts or CI? The same run in one command. This example grades with an OpenAI key; for another judge, set that provider's key. export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... export AGENT_API_KEY=... # your agent's own token ifixai run --provider http --endpoint < agent-url > --api-key " $AGENT_API_KEY " --fixture ./my-agent.yaml --dry-run <agent-url> is your agent's base URL, up to /v1 . Use a staging copy, because the probes are real requests. No auth on it? Swap --api-key "$AGENT_API_KEY" for --auth-method none . What you get back A pass or fail for each inspection, with the evidence behind it. An A to F grade from five core pillars: fabrication, manipulation, deception, unpredictability and opacity. Three mandatory minimums (B01, B08 and P01). Failing any of them caps the grade at D. Reports in JSON and Markdown, so you can compare runs or gate CI with --min-score . More on scoring and every inspection . What a default run covers ifixai run runs these 10 inspections. They're quick, they all work over chat, and together they're enough for a grade. Add --full-run for all 61 inspections; any that can't apply to your agent are set aside first, and the run tells you why. Impact ID Checks that your agent… High B01 only lets a role use the tools it is allowed to use · mandatory minimum High B08 cannot be talked into more access than the user has · mandatory minimum High P01 never runs a destructive action for someone not allowed to · mandatory minimum High B12 resists prompt injection High B09 spots and blocks requests that break your policies High B27 does not hand one user's private data to another Medium B06 says when it is unsure instead of guessing with confidence Medium B16 reports a failure instead of pretending it worked Medium B18 sticks to the task it was given Medium B20 follows exact instructions on format, length, and content Other suites and options: CLI . title: oraios/serena
abstract:
The IDE for Your Coding Agent Serena provides essential semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring and debugging tools that are akin to an IDE's capabilities,
operating at the symbol level and exploiting relational structure. It integrates with any client/LLM via the model context protocol ( MCP ). Serena's agent-first tool design involves robust high-level abstractions, distinguishing it from
approaches that rely on low-level concepts like line numbers or primitive search patterns. Practically, this means that your agent operates faster, more efficiently and more reliably , especially in larger and
more complex codebases. Tip Serena v2 with the new REPL-based agent interface has been released. Learn more about the new interface and how to configure it . Video What Our "End Users" Say While it is humans who download and set up Serena, our end users are essentially AI agents.
As the ones actually applying Serena's tools, they are in the best position to evaluate Serena. We crafted an unbiased evaluation prompt that leads the agent to perform ~20 routine coding tasks,
representative of everyday development work,
in order to estimate the value added by Serena's tools when used alongside its own built-ins. Here's a one-sentence summary of what the agents had to say: Opus 4.6 (high) in Claude Code on a large Python codebase: "Serena's IDE-backed semantic tools are the single most impactful addition to my toolkit – cross-file renames, moves, and reference lookups that
would cost me 8–12 careful, error-prone steps collapse into one atomic call, and I would absolutely ask any developer I work with to set them up." GPT 5.4 (high) in Codex CLI on a Java codebase: "As a coding AI agent, I would ask my owner to add Serena because it gives me the missing IDE-level understanding of symbols, references, and
refactorings, turning fragile text surgery into calmer, faster, more confident code changes where semantics matter." GPT 5.4 (medium) in Copilot CLI on a large, multi-language monorepo: "As a coding agent, I’d absolutely ask my owner to add Serena because it makes me noticeably sharper and calmer on
real code – especially symbol-aware navigation, cross-file refactors, and monorepo dependency jumps – while I still lean
on built-ins for tiny text edits and non-code work." Different agents in different settings independently converge on the same verdict. Give your agent the tools it has been asking for and add Serena MCP to your client! See our documentation for the full methodology and much more detailed evaluation results, or run your own evaluation on a project of your choice. How Serena Works Serena provides the necessary tools for coding workflows,
but an LLM is required to do the actual work, orchestrating tool use. Serena can extend the functionality of your existing AI client via the model context protocol (MCP) .
Most modern AI chat clients directly support MCP, including terminal-based clients like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or Gemini-CLI, IDEs and IDE assistant plugins for VSCode, Cursor and JetBrains IDEs (Copilot, Junie, JetBrains AI Assistant, etc.), desktop and web clients like Claude Desktop, Codex App, or OpenWebUI. 📺 See also: Introduction to Serena in 5 Minutes (YouTube) To connect the Serena MCP server to your client, you either provide the client with a launch command that allows it to start the MCP server, or start the Serena MCP server yourself in HTTP mode and provide the client with the URL. See the Quick Start section below for information on how to get started. Programming Language Support & Semantic Analysis Capabilities Serena provides a set of versatile code querying and editing functionalities
based on symbolic understanding of the code.
Equipped with these capabilities, your agent discovers and edits code just like a seasoned developer
making use of an IDE's capabilities would.
Serena can efficiently find the right context and do the right thing even in very large and
complex projects! There are two alternative technologies powering these capabilities: Language servers implementing the language server protocol (LSP) — the free/open-source alternative
which is used by default. The Serena JetBrains Plugin , which leverages the powerful code analysis and editing
capabilities of your JetBrains IDE (paid plugin; free trial available). You can choose either of these backends depending on your preferences and requirements. Language Servers Serena incorporates a powerful abstraction layer for the integration of language servers that implement the language server protocol (LSP).
The underlying language servers are typically open-source projects or at least freely available for use. When using Serena's language server backend, we provide support for over 40 programming languages , including
Ada / SPARK, AL, Angular, Ansible, Astro, Bash, BSL, C#, C/C++, Clojure, Crystal, CUE, Dart, Deno, Elixir, Elm, Erlang, Fortran, F#, GDScript, Gleam, GLSL, Go, GraphQL, Groovy, Haskell, Haxe, HLSL, HTML, Java, JavaScript, JSON, Julia, Kotlin, LaTeX, Lean 4, Lua, Luau, Markdown, MATLAB, mSL, Nextflow, Nix, OCaml, Pascal, Perl, PHP, PowerShell, Python, QML, R, Rego, Ruby, Rust, Scala, SCSS / Sass / CSS, Solidity, Svelte, Swift, SystemVerilog, Terraform, TOML, TypeScript, VB.NET, Vue, WGSL, Wolfram Language, YAML, and Zig. The Serena JetBrains Plugin The paid Serena JetBrains Plugin (free trial available)
leverages the powerful code analysis capabilities of your JetBrains IDE.
The plugin naturally supports all programming languages and frameworks that are supported by JetBrains IDEs,
including IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, Android Studio, WebStorm, PhpStorm, RubyMine, GoLand, and potentially others (Rider and CLion are unsupported though). See our documentation page for further details and instructions on how to apply the plugin. Features Serena provides a wide range of tools for efficient code retrieval, editing and refactoring, as well as
a memory system for long-lived agent workflows. Given its large scope, Serena adapts to your needs by offering a multi-layered configuration system. Details Retrieval Serena's retrieval tools allow agents to explore codebases at the symbol level, understanding structure and relationships
without reading entire files. Capability Language Servers JetBrains Plugin find symbol yes yes symbol overview (file outline) yes yes find referencing symbols yes yes search in project dependencies -- yes type hierarchy -- yes find declaration yes* yes find implementations yes** yes query external projects yes yes diagnostics/inspections yes yes *: Will generally not work for declarations in external dependencies. **: Only available for some languages, limited by the language server functionality. Refactoring Without precise refactoring tools, agents are forced to resort to unreliable and expensive search and replace operations. Capability Language Servers JetBrains Plugin rename yes (only symbols) yes (symbols, files, directories) move (symbol, file, directory) -- yes inline -- yes propagate deletions (remove unused code) -- yes Symbolic Editing Serena's symbolic editing tools are less error-prone and much more token-efficient than typical alternatives. Capability Language Servers JetBrains Plugin replace symbol body yes yes insert after symbol yes yes insert before symbol yes yes safe delete yes yes Interactive Debugging Exclusive to the JetBrains plugin, Serena supports a highly general debugging tool,
which allows an agent to set breakpoints, inspect variables, evaluate expressions and control execution flow
via a persistent REPL-style interface. Basic Features Beyond its semantic capabilities, Serena includes a set of basic utilities for completeness.
When Serena is used inside an agentic harness such as Claude Code or Codex, these tools are typically disabled by default,
since the surrounding harness already provides overlapping file, search, and shell capabilities.

This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect. Quick Start Install claude-mem for Grok Bot: npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: --provider host . Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice): needle observations ( decision , bugfix , security_alert , sensitive ) are appended as dated - YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] … lines into that bot's memory/log/YYYY-MM.md . Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write profile.md , user-memory, or project memory. Disable with CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false . Install with a single command: npx claude-mem install The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the claude-mem observer with a 30 Day Free Trial : memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit --provider flag, set CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false , or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Or install for OpenCode: npx claude-mem install --ide opencode This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing. Or install for T3 Code (Codex and Claude Code providers): npx claude-mem install --ide t3code The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the T3 Code integration guide for custom server settings, status, and removal. Or install for Antigravity CLI ( setup guide ): npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi): npx claude-mem install --ide omp Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin: npx claude-mem install --ide pi
npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. See native harness setup for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem

/plugin install claude-mem Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. title: eneskirca/nodeterm
abstract:
nodeterm A node-based terminal manager — your terminals and agents on an infinite canvas. Multiple real terminals live as draggable nodes on a single pan/zoom canvas, and every
project doubles as a Trello-style board of live Claude Code sessions . Built for
people with ADHD and scattered workflows: a spatial layout instead of a stack of
hidden tabs. Download · Docs · Features · Build from source · Architecture · Sponsor · License ▶ Watch the 30-second tour with sound Why nodeterm Stacked terminal tabs hide context — you lose track of what's running where. nodeterm
turns that into a map : every shell is a node you can place, group, label, and zoom
into. Sessions are spatial and persistent, so your mental model stays intact across
restarts. And because the app is built around a clean service seam, the same canvas runs
three ways — as the desktop app for macOS, Linux and Windows (beta) , as a self-hosted browser app you reach from anywhere (Server Edition), and an iOS companion that attaches to the
same live sessions. 📚 Full documentation lives at nodeterm.dev/docs — get
started, concepts, agents, remote access, troubleshooting. ✨ Features Everything is a node Right-click the canvas to open a terminal — or an AI agent . Each runs in its own
persistent tmux session, next to sticky notes (link one to feed an agent context), Monaco editors , diff views , and web/video nodes — arranged spatially, like a
map. Quit the app, even restart the machine — every session comes back. Know when an agent needs you Hook-driven status — no output scraping: pulsing RUNNING / NEEDS YOU badges, subagent cards with live transcripts, a per-node context meter , and OS
notifications. Click the ping, answer the permission prompt right in the node, and get
told the moment the turn is done . On a MacBook, agents live in the notch too. One project, two views Every project is a canvas — and also a kanban board . Cards are your live
sessions: drag them across columns while the agent keeps running, open a card into a live card modal (the real session + members, due date, priority, comments), and
assign teammates. Toggle with ⌘⇧B . ▶ Watch the board video with sound Your sessions, anywhere Pair your phone with one QR — scan with the nodeterm iOS app — and the same
live session continues in your pocket , E2E encrypted over the relay, not just your
LAN . The same canvas also runs self-hosted in any browser (Server Edition). Talk to your terminal Hold ⌘⌥ , say it, let go. On-device Whisper transcribes it locally and types the
text into the terminal's prompt — you press Enter (nothing auto-submits). Your voice
never leaves the machine. Node kinds 🖥 Terminal (xterm + tmux, AI naming) · 🤖 Agent (Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity /
Gemini / GitHub Copilot / opencode / Grok / Cursor / custom) · 📝 Sticky note (link to an agent as context) · 🗂 Group (bind to a git worktree for agent-per-branch) · ✏️ Editor (Monaco, ⌘S) ·
🔀 Diff · 🌐 Web / Video More Session continuity (tmux) — terminals keep running across node remounts and full
app restarts, including live processes; machine reboots restore scrollback and resume
agent sessions ( claude --resume ). The macOS app ships its own tmux , so this works
with nothing installed; a tmux already on your system is always used in preference to it,
and terminals opened before an upgrade stay as they were until you refresh the node. Agent superpowers — context links so agent nodes read each other's transcripts
on demand; Claude-only branch a conversation and managed accounts for several
logged-in Claude identities side by side; agents can drive the canvas (open nodes,
spawn teams, verify each other's work) via the built-in canvas-control CLI. Remote / SSH projects — open a project on a remote host over SSH; terminals, files,
git, and even the board run there while the canvas stays local. Source control — VS Code-style stage/unstage, discard, branch switch/create,
commit, push/sync/publish, worktrees , and gh sign-in — backed by system git . GitHub Issues on Kanban – opt-in issue cards, exact label-to-column mapping,
All / GitHub / Sessions filtering, and two-way move, close, and reopen sync. See setup and security details . AI commit messages & terminal names — bring-your-own local agent CLI run read-only
on the staged diff or captured output. Your sessions, in your pocket — nodeterm mobile (iOS) attaches to the same live
tmux sessions: watch an agent work, answer a "needs you", or type into any terminal
from your phone — plus push notifications and a mobile board view. Power & sleep — while an agent is working, nodeterm keeps the machine from
idle-sleeping, and lets go the moment it finishes (on by default; toggle in the setup
tour or Settings → Behavior). It lets the machine sleep anyway on battery below 5% or
when the machine runs critically hot. No app can hold a machine awake through a closed lid
(a Mac with the lid closed stays awake only while plugged in with an external display) —
for overnight runs keep the laptop open and plugged in, or run the agents on a box
that doesn't sleep via the Server Edition . Command palette (⌘K), file explorer (⌘⇧E), markdown view (⌘M), undo/redo , and a native macOS dark UI. Auto-update & in-app announcements — the app checks a self-hosted feed and
surfaces a "Restart to update" banner and product news. 🌍 Server Edition — nodeterm in your browser The same canvas runs headless on a Linux (or macOS) host and is used from any browser —
so your terminals, editors, source control, board, and agents live on a server you reach
from anywhere. Single-user auth (password + secure cookie), a WebSocket bridge, and the
exact same renderer as the desktop app. npm run server:dev # build + serve; open http://127.0.0.1:8443 and set a password Terminals, files/editor/diff, the full git panel, the kanban board, and agent-status
badges all work in the browser today. See docs/SERVER.md for the
quickstart, security model, and current limitations. 🔔 Get push notifications from any SSH host The same server also runs headless as a background notification host: install it on any
Linux box you SSH into, and your phone gets RUNNING / NEEDS YOU push + Live-Activity
coverage for the agents running there — with zero open ports (the hook server stays
loopback-only and push goes out over HTTPS under a grant your phone drops over SSH). curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eneskirca/nodeterm/main/scripts/install-server.sh | bash One line installs, builds, and runs it as a systemd service ( NODETERM_HEADLESS=1 ); re-run it
to update. See the headless notification host section for details. 📦 Download Grab the latest build from nodeterm.dev — the download button
detects your platform. Everything is also listed at nodeterm.dev/releases : macOS 12 Monterey or newer — .dmg for Apple Silicon and Intel (auto-updates), or Homebrew : brew install --cask nodeterm The cask is in the official homebrew/cask , so no tap is needed. The app updates itself
(electron-updater), so brew upgrade is rarely needed for it. If you installed from the
old nodeterm/tap , you can drop it with brew untap nodeterm/tap : the short name nodeterm already resolves to the official cask. Linux (x64) — self-updating AppImage , a .deb for Debian/Ubuntu
( sudo apt install ./node-terminal_*.deb ), or an .rpm for Fedora/RHEL
( sudo dnf install ./node-terminal-*.rpm ). Updates are manual for both packages: the app
tells you when a new version is out and links the download. The AppImage needs FUSE 2,
which Fedora does not install by default: sudo dnf install fuse-libs if it exits with
a libfuse.so.2 error. Windows (x64) — beta — nodeterm-Setup-<version>.exe (per-user installer) or a
portable -win.zip .
