title: DWI: Efficient On-Device LLM Decoding Through Dynamic Width Selection on Nested Models
abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) on resource-constrained mobile devices remains a significant challenge due to memory limitations and high I/O overhead. While existing dynamic sparsity methods reduce computation costs, they often suffer from inefficient loading patterns that degrade I/O throughput. To address this, we propose to leverage dynamic width selection and optimized parameter management on nested models to enable efficient on-device LLM inference. Our approach introduces three key techniques: 1) an end-to-end dynamic width selection mechanism that optimizes nested LLMs’ width configurations across tokens to balance efficiency and quality, 2) a cyclic-locality-aware cache policy that dynamically evicts stale parameters to minimize redundant I/O, and 3) a block-wise load-computation pipeline that overlaps in-memory computation with loading from flash to mitigate I/O latency. Experimental results demonstrate that our method accelerates on-device LLM inference by up to <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$34\times$</tex-math><alternatives><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mn>34</mml:mn><mml:mo>×</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math><inline-graphic xlink:href="cao-ieq1-3711495.gif"/></alternatives></inline-formula>, while maintaining competitive model performance, making it a promising solution for on-device LLM deployment.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Large Language Models for Visual Question Answering of Construction Occupational Health and Safety Hazards
abstract: Construction occupational health and safety (OHS) hazard oversight is a critical pillar of engineering management, requiring the complex integration of dynamic visual evidence with rigorous regulatory standards. Traditional oversight, heavily reliant on manual inspections, is labor intensive and prone to cognitive omissions. While automated hazard detection has evolved, existing paradigms remain constrained by closed-set recognition, failing to simulate the open-ended, heuristic reasoning of safety experts. To bridge this gap, this study proposed a visual knowledge enhancement framework for construction OHS visual question answering (VQA) based on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). It can reliably respond to site managers’ open questions about OHS hazards in construction images. The method’s primary innovation lies in a tailored RAG framework with a knowledge base for construction OHS hazard VQA, addressing three critical challenges: cross-modal semantic misalignment, knowledge demand variability, and information overload–induced cognitive bias. To enable systematic evaluation of the framework and mitigate the lack of public benchmarks, we designed experiments across three question types and built the Construction Hazard VQA Dataset (ConHazard-VQA), the first dedicated dataset for construction OHS hazard VQA, featuring 1,034 high-quality image-question-answer pairs. Experiments across classification, counting, and open-ended question types confirmed consistent and significant performance gains over the baseline. By introducing a tailored, practical framework that translates a general-purpose MLLM into a domain-specific expert for construction OHS hazard VQA, a new paradigm for data-driven safety management was established. This research advances the body of knowledge in engineering management by transitioning automated oversight from rigid pattern matching to expert-like, diagnostic decision support, thereby augmenting managerial capacity for reliable and objective OHS hazard prevention.

title: A comparative review of modern large language model paradigms: GPT-4, BERT, Gemini, and DeepSeek
abstract: This review provides comparative analysis of GPT-4, BERT (bidirectional encoder representations from transformers), Gemini, and DeepSeek large language models (LLM), focusing architectures, training methodologies, and real-world applications. The primary research question is: How do these models differ in design, strengths, limitations, and potential areas for enhancement? By addressing this question, the study aims to provide insights into the trade-offs and future directions for optimizing LLM performance and deployment. The analysis reveals GPT-4 excels in natural language generation and complex reasoning, supporting up to 128K tokens with moderate latency and higher costs making it effective for conversational artificial intelligence (AI). BERT excels bidirectional contextual understanding with smaller computational overhead and broad open-source adoption, effective for text classification. Gemini demonstrates superior multimodal integration processing text, image, audio, and code with context lengths up to 1M tokens, enabling cross-domain adaptability. DeepSeek excels in specialized domains like finance and programming, is optimized for efficiency and supports extended context windows exceeding 200K tokens. However, all models face challenges related to computational cost, hallucinations, and ethical concerns, necessitating further improvements. Despite advancements, LLMs continue to grapple with issues such as data bias, model interpretability, and responsible AI deployment. Future research should focus on hybrid model approaches, domain-specific fine-tuning, and transparency to mitigate risks while maximizing the transformative potential of LLMs in real-world applications.

title: Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation with Uncertainty Alignment for Robotic Scene Understanding of Indoor Building Spaces
abstract: Society is steadily embracing the idea of coinhabitant service robots in the built environment for assistance with household tasks and chores. In particular, the growing number of older adults, individuals with disabilities, and people requiring daily assistance has further created an urgent need for intelligent coinhabitant robots capable of supporting mobility, independence, and safety within physical living spaces. The growing complexity of modern built environments and the increasing prevalence of coinhabitant robots have underscored the need for advanced computational methods to support analysis, monitoring, and management. To provide users with meaningful assistance and clear scene understanding in such settings, robots must be able to perceive, interpret, and reason about their surroundings in a way that aligns with human spatial understanding. Place segmentation, which delineates spatial regions such as rooms or functional areas, together with semantic recognition, which assigns meaningful labels to these regions, forms the basis for accurate scene understanding in building-scale environments. Existing deep learning approaches have largely relied on closed-vocabulary detection systems, which are limited to a predefined set of categories of rooms and therefore struggle to interpret diverse or naturalistic descriptions of spaces. Furthermore, most current methods neglect the uncertainty inherent in scene recognition—for example, when rooms have overlapping functions (e.g., kitchen–dining areas) or when people use linguistically similar descriptions to refer to distinct spaces—thereby reducing their effectiveness in ambiguous or complex environments. To address these challenges, we propose an open-vocabulary semantic segmentation and classification pipeline that leverages vision–language models (VLMs) and large language models. Our framework follows a “segment–detect–select” paradigm for open-vocabulary scene understanding, consisting of three modules: (1) segmentation of distinct rooms and regions in the scene; (2) VLM-based similarity scoring between descriptive queries and segmented regions; and (3) adaptive conformal prediction to select among candidate regions while explicitly accounting for uncertainty. Evaluation results on the large-scale Matterport3D dataset, which comprises diverse photorealistic indoor environments, show that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary methods in scene segmentation [by 30% in AP50 and 5% in mean intersection over union (mIOU)], classification (by 200% in F1 score and 263% in mean average precision), and selection (by 50% in room mIoU). These advances are significant for built environments, as improved scene understanding directly supports safer, more adaptive, and more intuitive coinhabitant assistive agents for humans in complex indoor spaces.

title: Congestion Propagation Identification and Prediction Using Self Attention–Based Diffusion Convolutional Approach
abstract:
Traffic congestion frequently propagates among the interconnected road networks over time, driven by spatial and temporal factors. Identifying and predicting these patterns is crucial for effective public transport management and urban planning. Existing systems often fail to accurately capture the complex diffusion properties of traffic flow and spatial dependencies, resulting in less reliable predictions. This study utilizes a propagation probability matrix to identify congestion propagation patterns and finds traffic behavior over 24 h, revealing critical insights into congestion trends in a selected road network. In addition, to overcome the remaining limitations, we propose a novel self attention–based diffusion convolutional network (SADCN) that effectively predicts traffic congestion propagation. The proposed model incorporates key spatial relations, including adjacency, diffusion, and propagation probability matrices, to improve the understanding of congestion dynamics. To demonstrate the significance of SADCN, we compare its performance with several recent graph-based models, including fully connected long short-term memory (FC-LSTM), diffusion convolutional recurrent neural network (DCRNN), and attention-based spatial-temporal graph convolutional network (ASTGCN). title: Kol-3-Freq: Frequency-Aware Video Deepfake Detection Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
abstract: Deepfake detection is a critical task today in multimedia forensics due to its unethical exploitation and serious consequences. Currently several deepfake detection techniques exist which involve synthetic human facial video detection, and most of which operate in the spatial domain While these methods are often very accurate (particularly, with respect to “in-dataset” analysis), none of them is foolproof, and are often susceptible to the sophistication of state-of-the-art deepfake generators. Very often, deepfakes generated by GANs, VAEs, or diffusion models are spatio-temporally coherent, but show prominent inconsistencies in the spectral domain. In this paper we propose <sc>Kol-3-Freq</sc>, a set of three neural deepfake detectors that detect frequency domain inconsistencies to classify real and synthetic videos. <sc>Kol-3-Freq</sc> models built on the novel Kolmogorov-Arnold Network, which makes the model architecture (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\approx 2.181$ </tex-math></inline-formula> times) <italic>lightweight</italic> and more <italic>interpretable</italic> compared to the state-of-the-art, besides achieving a competitive performance improvement (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\approx 1.4106\%$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) to its primitives when evaluated on standard deepfake datasets. <sc>Kol-3-Freq</sc> is further extended to four tiers–<sc>Light</sc>, <sc>Base</sc>, <sc>Large</sc>, and <sc>Huge</sc>, based on handling input-feature dimensionality of the underlying Kolmogorov-Arnold Network, making them <italic>adaptive</italic> and <italic>robust</italic>.

title: DDPM-Driven Background Suppression for Efficient and Accurate Hyperspectral Anomaly Change Detection
abstract: Hyperspectral anomaly change detection aims to precisely capture the subtle spectral differences between multitemporal hyperspectral images (HSIs) in order to accurately identify changes on the Earth’s surface. However, this field faces numerous challenges. On one hand, differences in imaging conditions of multitemporal HSIs lead to the confusion between real surface changes and pseudo changes caused by variations in imaging conditions. On the other hand, significant background differences in multitemporal HSIs result in poor performance of traditional background suppression methods. In light of these challenges, this paper applies Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) to the field of background suppression in hyperspectral anomaly change detection and proposes a novel unsupervised hyperspectral change detection algorithm—DDPM-Driven Background Suppression Method (DDBS). DDBS employs a background reconstruction-suppression hybrid processing structure. It reduces the background differences between multi-temporal HSIs through the background reconstruction process and simulates the common background of bi-temporal hyperspectral images through a novel DDPMs noise generation method. During the inference process, the common background is removed as noise, thereby suppressing the common background in multi-temporal HSIs and highlighting anomalous changes. Furthermore, the proposed hybrid background reconstruction-suppression architecture only requires a single inference step to effectively suppress common background components in multitemporal HSIs. Experimental results on multiple public datasets demonstrate that the proposed DDBS outperforms state-of-the-art background reconstruction and suppression methods in hyperspectral anomaly change detection tasks.

title: Multimodal GenAI for Scalable Synthetic Dataset Generation in Autonomous Vehicles: Advancements, Challenges, and Opportunities in Intelligent Transportation Systems [Feature Article: Generative AI for Synthetic Dataset Generation]
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is emerging as a transformative tool for synthetic dataset generation in advanced driver-assistance systems (ADASs). Traditional autonomous vehicle (AV) datasets face high collection costs, limited edge-case diversity, and scalability challenges, making alternative data generation approaches essential. This article introduces an innovative application of multimodal GenAI models for AV perception tasks with a focus on ADAS applications. Specifically, the study explores text-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video, and image-to-image models to generate high-fidelity data for object detection, segmentation, and trajectory prediction. Despite their promise, practical deployment is obstructed by prompt adherence failures, mode collapse, uncontrollability, domain adaptation inconsistencies, and computational inefficiencies. We provide a comparative evaluation of these models, benchmarking their realism, consistency, and adaptability in bridging the synthetic-to-real gap and enhancing AV robustness. Experimental results highlight the strengths and limitations of different approaches, with insights into controllable data synthesis and improvements in real-time efficiency. Furthermore, YOLO models fine-tuned on GenAI-generated datasets achieve superior detection performance, with GAI_YOLOv7 reaching 74.48% mean average precision (mAP) and GAI_YOLOv8x achieving 76.16% mAP, outperforming virtual reality-based models (29.76%, 23.44%).

title: Poster: Evaluating LLM Agents for Post-Quantum Cryptographic Migrations
abstract: No benchmark measures whether large language model agents can correctly add post-quantum cryptography, or PQC, to a real codebase. We present an early version of PQCMigrate-Bench, a benchmark that builds each task from a range of open-source commits that added a PQC algorithm. The agent receives the repository at the start of the range, and its patch is graded in an isolated container against held-out tests taken from the same range. The current set has 10 instances in Java, Go, Rust, Python, TypeScript, and C++ projects. In a first sweep of four models with the Inspect AI ReAct agent, 25 of 40 runs resolved their task, and every instance was resolved by at least one model.

title: Deep Generative Model-Aided Communication-Efficient and Cyber-Resilient Power System Dynamic State Estimation
abstract: Fast and robust dynamic state estimation (DSE) is critical for capturing the internal dynamics of cyber-physical power systems. Traditional model-based approaches, such as Kalman filtering and particle filtering, require accurate parameters, control inputs, phasor measurement unit (PMU) data, and reliable centralized communication. These dependencies make them vulnerable to accuracy bottlenecks under structural or process errors, unknown control vectors, cyberattacks, and communication contingencies. In contrast, deep learning-aided DSE eliminates parameter dependence but often suffers from limited generalization under unforeseen operating conditions. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a deep generative model-aided framework with AI-generated content (AIGC) for error-bounded DSE. The framework integrates an encoder-decoder architecture to estimate unknown control inputs, a robust encoder to suppress PMU anomalies, and a latent diffusion model to mitigate communication issues in centralized DSE. In addition, a lightweight adaptor is introduced to rapidly adjust latent vector distributions under unforeseen contingencies and moderate topology variations. Extensive experiments on the IEEE 39-bus and NPCC 140-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method effectively addresses modeling imperfections, measurement uncertainties, communication contingencies, and distribution shifts, while also reducing storage and communication requirements. Overall, the proposed error-bounded approach provides a powerful complement to model-based DSE methods dominated by Kalman filtering (KF).

title: LLM-Based Intrusion and Anomaly Detection for IoT Networks: A Systematic Survey
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to intrusion detection in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, yet their practical deployability, robustness, and evaluability remain largely undemonstrated. This article presents a preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA)-based systematic survey of LLM-driven IoT intrusion detection published between 2022 and 2026. A taxonomy is introduced spanning functional roles, model architectures, learning paradigms, deployment models, traffic representations, resource awareness, and robustness evaluation, applied to 122 fully classified studies. Through corpus-wide quantitative analysis, three evaluation gaps in the current research landscape are identified: 1) a deployment gap—38.5% of studies evaluate in explicitly cloud-hosted settings and a further 33.6% omit deployment context entirely; together, 72.1% provide no evidence of IoT edge feasibility and fewer than 14% report inference latency; 2) a comparability crisis—no single benchmark is shared by more than five LLM-based papers, and 73% of studies report accuracy without macro-F1 or per-class recall, rendering cross-study comparison methodologically unreliable; and 3) adversarial blindness—89.3% of approaches are never evaluated under adversarial conditions despite operating in inherently adversarial environments. These findings suggest that current evaluation practices prioritize benchmark accuracy more consistently than deployment-oriented dimensions such as edge feasibility, adversarial robustness, and evaluation comparability. To address this, a minimum evaluation protocol (MEP-IoT-LLM) is proposed, and a research roadmap is outlined, targeting the critically underexplored intersection of edge deployment, adversarial robustness, and continual learning.

title: Trustworthy Collaborative Agents for Industrial IoT: A Multimodal Mixed Reality Framework for Human-Centric Precision Assembly
abstract: In the evolving industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), the complexity of assembly tasks requires intelligent agents capable of augmenting human capabilities through real-time perception and decision-making. However, deploying such agents on edge devices faces challenges in spatial alignment accuracy and computational efficiency, which compromise their trustworthiness in high-risk environments. To address these issues, this article proposes a human-centric collaborative agent (HC-CoAgent), a lightweight mixed reality (MR) framework tailored for precision circuit assembly. Unlike traditional static systems, HC-CoAgent functions as a “cognitive peer”—an AI partner that dynamically shares the operator’s cognitive load by fusing visual object recognition, gesture tracking, and gaze input. Crucially, to bridge the “reality gap,” we introduce a novel human-in-the-loop (HITL) spatial alignment mechanism utilizing a threshold-controlled 3-D pointing strategy. The theoretical rigor of this mechanism is validated via a support vector machine (SVM) analysis, which defines the precise trustworthiness boundaries for safe interaction. Furthermore, visual attention analysis reveals that the agent functions as a cognitive anchor, significantly reducing visual entropy and aligning novice gaze patterns with expert baselines. Experimental results from industrial wiring scenarios demonstrate that HC-CoAgent improves task efficiency by 33% and reduces error rates significantly compared to both traditional paper-based methods and uncalibrated MR baselines. The system also exhibits low cognitive load and high usability, validating its potential as an effective and efficient edge AI agent for empowering the IIoT workforce.

title: Efficient VLM Inference System With LoRA Adapters at the Edge
abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) extend large language models with visual perception, enabling complex vision tasks at the edge. Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) adapters offer a lightweight method to inject domain-specific knowledge into a shared base VLM, making them attractive for edge serving where concurrent mobile clients require diverse specialized capabilities. However, existing LoRA serving systems, designed primarily for text workloads, fail to meet the efficiency and accuracy demands of vision applications: heterogeneous adapter batching incurs excessive padding waste, mode-switch mechanisms clash with modern serving techniques causing request starvation, and no principled method exists for generating accuracy-guaranteed adapters. We present VaLoRA, an end-to-end LoRA VLM serving system that addresses these challenges with three techniques. First, an accuracy-aware adapter generator formulates adapter creation as constrained bin packing and pairs it with a hierarchical runtime router for automatic request dispatch. Second, an Adaptive-Tiling Matrix Multiplication (ATMM) operator eliminates padding waste by selecting optimal tiling configurations for concurrent heterogeneous adapters. Third, a flexible orchestrator enables swift mode switching and mixture inference to satisfy diverse latency and throughput requirements without request starvation. Evaluation on five vision tasks across three VLMs shows that VaLoRA improves accuracy by 24–62% over original VLMs and reduces latency by 20–89% compared to S-LoRA, Punica, and dLoRA.

title: A Hybrid Knowledge-Enhanced Legal AI System for Construction Contract Disputes
abstract: With rapid urbanization and expanding infrastructure, construction contract disputes are increasing in volume and complexity, challenging traditional adjudication. This study proposes a domain-specific legal artificial intelligence (AI) system for construction contract disputes via hybrid knowledge integration based on the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) paradigm, integrating five core legal texts and 500 adjudication cases within a dual-engine architecture. The knowledge base encodes legal concepts, relations, and rules to enable structured semantic inference. The DeepSeek-R1 reasoning engine analyzes case facts and legal logic via constrained generation, while the BGE-M3 retrieval module matches legal provisions and precedents using multivector indexing. A tripartite evaluation framework—semantic similarity, legal provision citation accuracy, and issue prediction F1 score—validates system performance. The hybrid knowledge model outperforms single-source models, achieving scores of 0.736, 0.952, and 0.937, respectively, while significantly reducing judicial document generation time. This study offers a theoretical and empirical basis for legal AI in Chinese construction disputes, demonstrating how integrating diverse legal knowledge enhances intelligent judicial assistance within China’s jurisdiction. It also provides a scalable methodological reference for the advancement of smart justice, with explicit recognition of its current jurisdictional limitations.

title: PGDNet: Prior Guided Dual-Domain Fusion Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
abstract: Infrared small target detection remains unreliable in cluttered scenes. Small target structures are easily degraded during cross-scale feature propagation, and their weak responses are often overwhelmed by background-dominant spectra. In addition, attention mechanisms tend to be biased toward salient clutter when target saliency is extremely low. We propose a Prior Guided Dual-Domain Fusion Network for infrared small target detection, in which semantic priors from a vision foundation model guide adaptive spatial–spectral fusion for robust target localization in cluttered scenes. PGDNet designs a Dynamic Structure-Constrained Diffusion Mechanism (DSCDM) to stabilize cross-scale propagation and preserve the spatial integrity of small targets. Built upon this structure-consistent representation, PGDNet develops Spectral Channel Selection Attention (SCSA) to enhance target-relevant frequency responses and suppress background interference. On this basis, cross-region attention priors are learned by fine-tuning DINOv3 and are integrated through a curriculum adaptive fusion(CAF) strategy to regulate prior influence and maintain stable guidance during training. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that PGDNet consistently achieves the best mIoU (78.83 / 94.64 / 75.50 in NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K), while maintaining a favorable balance between $P_{d}$ and $F_{a}$ under complex backgrounds. Our code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Eureka10086/PGDNet

title: Inferring Spatial Reasoning by Observing Human Interactions With Smart IoT Objects
abstract: This paper presents a proof-of-concept for a new paradigm for analyzing human-object interactions with high spatiotemporal resolution. The system comprises a set of smart IoT objects, equipped with sensors to monitor their spatial states and surroundings, including other smart objects. Each object is able to detect, store, and wirelessly report its orientation, rotation, adjacency, and various types of movements, both its own and those of neighboring objects. By collating this data, an analytical model can reconstruct a participant’s spatiotemporal handling of the objects with millisecond resolution, thereby inferring their spatial reasoning process. The objective is to establish a IoT echo systems for monitoring, characterizing, and enhancing human spatial reasoning through this novel approach of observing interactions between humans and objects with agency. The paper delves into the engineering details of the IoT system, followed by a series of spatial reasoning-related experiments. Subsequently, analytical methods are developed to gain insights into participants’ spatial reasoning within the context of two well-known tasks: the Tower of Hanoi and the Wechsler Block Design Task. Finally, the results are presented to demonstrate the practicality of the developed IoT-style smart object system for quantitatively understanding spatial reasoning in a data-driven manner.
